title: Digital Economy Policy and National Competitiveness: Nigeria and China in Perspective
summary: The study compared the digital economy policies of Nigeria and China to examine how differences in policy design influence national competitiveness. Specifically, it analysed Nigeria’s National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy (NDEPS 2020–2030) and China’s Digital China Construction Overall Layout Plan (2023–2035) with a view to understanding their institutional structures, governance arrangements, and implementation models. Guided by Policy Capacity Theory, the study adopted a qualitative method through a comparative policy analysis, drawing on official policy documents, government reports, and relevant scholarly literature. It was found that Nigeria’s digital economy strategy is largely market-driven and relies on private sector participation, public-private partnerships, and external financing. This approach contributed to improvements in digital inclusion, broadband expansion, and fintech development, challenges relating to institutional coordination, infrastructure gaps, and limited public investment constrain competitiveness. China’s strategy built around centralised coordination, state-directed financing, and long-term technological planning enabled the country to develop advanced digital infrastructure, strengthen innovation capacity, and position itself as a leading actor in emerging technologies. The study concluded that national competitiveness in the digital economy is shaped not only by the existence of digital policies but also by the coherence of policy design, governance structures, and implementation capacity. It therefore recommended that Nigeria strengthen institutional coordination, improve strategic public investment in digital infrastructure, and develop a more integrated framework for long-term digital transformation.

title: ESG Practices and SME Performance in Surabaya: Moderating Effects of Digital Transformation and Government Support
summary: This study examines the effect of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices on SME performance in Surabaya, Indonesia, and evaluates the moderating roles of digital transformation and government support. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data from 100 Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SME) owners and managers were collected through purposive sampling and analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4. The measurement model met reliability and validity criteria after removing two weak ESG indicators. ESG practices positively affected SME performance (β=0.348, t=3.137, p=0.002), and government support also had a significant effect (β=0.342, t=3.621, p<0.001), while digital transformation showed a positive but non-significant effect (β=0.219, t=1.802, p=0.072). The moderating effects of digital transformation (β=0.108, t=1.423, p=0.155) and government support (β=-0.085, t=0.863, p=0.388) were not significant. The model explained 51.3% of SME performance variance (R²=0.513) and showed positive predictive relevance (Q² predict=0.457). This study is limited by its cross-sectional design and focus on SMEs in a single urban context, which may affect generalizability. The findings contribute to the resource-based and dynamic-capability perspectives by demonstrating that ESG and government support directly enhance SME performance, while digital transformation does not automatically strengthen ESG outcomes.

title: Trade and environment governance at the World Trade Organization Committee on Trade and Environment
summary: This PHD reviews the work of the WTO Committee on Trade and Environment and the work outputs that have been generated throughout its 21 years of its existence, and utilizes three theoretical frameworks to aid the analysis and appreciation of the processes and seeming paucity of new rules for trade and environment governance. The work also examines the coherence / conflict dilemma arising from the committee’s tradedevelopment- environment triple-win mandate in the market access area. The research emphasizes the IL-IR dynamic of environmental rule-making and environmental governance that requires a balancing of the three competing frameworks of singular global governance, increased expert and professional bureaucracy, or more community-based localized solutions and multi-faceted institution-building.

title: Capital Market Opening-up and High-Quality Innovation of Enterprises
summary: At present, China’s innovation field is facing the structural dilemma of quantity priority and insufficient quality. In the critical window period when the economy turns to high-quality development, the improvement of enterprise innovation level has become an important issue. Based on the quasi-natural experimental scenario of capital market opening, this paper constructs a multi-period difference-in-differences model to test the effect of capital market opening on the quality of enterprise innovation. Both theoretical deduction and empirical test show that capital market opening helps to improve the quality of enterprise innovation, and this effect is more significant in state-owned enterprises and enterprises with overseas business income. From the perspective of mechanism, on the one hand, the opening of capital market promotes the improvement of innovation quality by improving corporate governance and alleviating financing bottlenecks ; on the other hand, due to the increase of stock liquidity, the quality of innovation is suppressed. Overall, the positive effect is dominant. This paper not only expands the theoretical analysis of the relationship between capital market opening and enterprise innovation, but also provides a useful reference for policy practice.

title: Blockchain Traceability and Visual Warning Based on Merkle Tree in Enterprise Data Assetization Transformation
summary: Large enterprise groups face issues such as low efficiency in data traceability and a disconnect between security and visualization in their data assetization transformation. Therefore, this paper raises a security threat perception and visualization warning model based on data visualization and blockchain traceability algorithm. This model combines Merkle Tree (MT), double hash chain, attribute encryption, and zero knowledge proof to achieve lightweight on chain auditing and privacy protection. It also collaborates with ForceTars2 and layered edge binding layout to generate dynamic risk topology, supporting full lifecycle trusted auditing and real-time threat perception. The experiment on the self-made enterprise supply chain threat perception dataset shows that the threat detection rate of the model is 98.11%, the false alarm rate is only 0.82%, the visual cognitive efficiency is 96.83%, the trusted data asset utilization rate is 96.82%, and the delay is controlled within 100 ms. Superior to existing mainstream solutions such as lightweight tracking algorithms based on MT and attribute based encryption privacy protection algorithms. The experimental results demonstrate that the model has good accuracy and applicability in enterprise level data security governance, providing an integrated governance solution with high concurrency, low latency, and high trustworthiness for data assetization transformation.

title: Pengaruh Mekanisme Internal Corporate Governance terhadap Tingkat Leverage Keuangan pada Perusahaan Manufaktur yang Terdaftar di BEI Periode 2022-2024
summary: This study aims to test and analyze the influence of the internal corporate governance mechanism consisting of an independent board of commissioners, managerial ownership, institutional ownership, and audit committee on the level of financial leverage (Debt to Equity Ratio) in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2022-2024 period. This study uses a quantitative approach with a sample of 57 companies selected through the purposive sampling method. The analysis technique used is panel data regression with a Random Effect Model (REM) model based on the results of the Chow Test, Hausman Test, and Langrange Multiplier Test. The results of the study show that simultaneously the four independent variables have a significant effect on leverage. However, partially, only institutional ownership has a negative and significant effect on leverage, while independent board of commissioners and managerial ownership have no significant effect on the negative direction, and the audit committee does not have a significant effect on the positive direction. These findings indicate that institutional investors have a more effective supervisory role than other internal governance mechanisms in controlling corporate debt policies.

title: Mobilizing climate finance for livestock transformation in the Global South
summary: Livestock systems sustain more than one billion people worldwide, most of them in low- and middle-income countries, making the sector central to food security, nutrition, and rural livelihoods across the Global South. At the same time, livestock accounts for roughly one fifth of agricultural greenhouse gas emissions, primarily methane. With global demand for animal sourced foods projected to double by 2050, countries face a dual imperative to raise productivity and resilience while substantially reducing emissions. Climate finance provides a practical pathway to address this challenge. By mobilizing public, blended, and private capital, governments can reduce the risk of investments in improved forages, enhanced grazing management, and low emission feed and manure systems. Such investments can simultaneously increase productivity, strengthen adaptive capacity, and generate measurable mitigation outcomes. Evidence from CGIAR and partners shows that sustainable intensification can reduce emission intensity by up to half while increasing yields and farm incomes. Proven technologies are already available, but financial mechanisms and institutional capacity to scale them remain insufficient. Transforming livestock systems therefore requires: A. Policy alignment, integrating livestock into national climate strategies, Nationally Determined Contributions, and investment plans. B. Robust monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) systems that produce credible and transparent data to confirm results and attract investment. C. Blended finance instruments that strategically combine concessional, private, and results-based funding to mobilize capital at scale. For African member states, the key policy task is to integrate livestock into national climate and investment frameworks, build credible MRV systems, and develop bankable livestock programs that can access concessional, blended, and results-based finance. Donors and research institutions play a complementary role by providing the data, standards, and tools that make livestock projects auditable, investable, and scalable. When governance, data, and finance converge, livestock can shift from being perceived mainly as a source of emissions to becoming a driver of low carbon, climate resilient growth and a strategic development opportunity for the Global South.

title: Digital Transformation in Retail Banking: Fintech's Effect on Service Quality and Customer Satisfaction in Mumbai
summary: Abstract: Introduction The rapid diffusion of financial technology (fintech) has fundamentally reshaped the delivery of retail banking services across urban India, with Mumbai the country's financial capital serving as an early adopter of digital banking innovation. Mobile banking applications, the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), robo-advisory tools, artificial-intelligence-driven chatbots and contactless payment systems have altered the manner in which customers interact with banks, raising important questions about how these technologies shape perceived service quality and, in turn, customer satisfaction. Purpose This study examines the extent to which fintech adoption influences the five SERVQUAL dimensions of service quality reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy and tangibles and overall customer satisfaction among retail banking customers in Mumbai. Methodology A descriptive and analytical research design was adopted. Primary data were collected from a sample of 100 retail banking customers in Mumbai through a structured questionnaire administered on a five-point Likert scale, supplemented by secondary data drawn from journals, RBI publications, NPCI reports and bank disclosures. Percentage analysis, mean analysis and Karl Pearson's correlation analysis were used to examine the relationships in the data. Findings Fintech adoption was found to be positively associated with customer-perceived service quality and satisfaction, with responsiveness and convenience-related dimensions showing the strongest association among Mumbai's retail banking customers. Respondents in the 21–40 age group and those with higher digital literacy reported significantly greater satisfaction with fintech-enabled banking channels than with traditional branch banking. All three hypotheses were statistically confirmed: a one-sample t-test showed fintech adoption is significantly related to perceived service quality (t = 12.46, p = 0.000); Karl Pearson's correlation confirmed a strong positive relationship between fintech-driven service quality and customer satisfaction (r = 0.72, p = 0.000); and a one-way ANOVA confirmed that satisfaction differs significantly across age groups (F = 3.85, p = 0.012). Implications The findings carry implications for retail banks seeking to refine digital-channel strategy, for regulators concerned with consumer protection and digital financial inclusion, and for future researchers seeking to extend the service-quality literature into the fintech domain.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Carbon Efficiency in the Airline Industry: Implications for Sustainability and Corporate Value
summary: The airline industry faces increasing pressure to balance economic performance with social and environmental responsibilities. This study investigates the influence of corporate social responsibility (CSR) on corporate value, incorporating the moderating role of carbon performance and the mediating effect of customer perception. A comprehensive CSR assessment framework based on ISO 26000 is developed across six dimensions: organizational governance, labor practices, the environment, consumer issues, fair operating practices, and community involvement. Panel data from 20 global airlines over 2017–2024 are used to test the proposed relationships. The results indicate that higher CSR scores are positively associated with corporate value and that customer perception, measured through Skytrax ratings, provides partial mediation. In addition, lower unit carbon intensity strengthens the positive CSR–value relationship, highlighting the importance of verifiable carbon performance in improving the financial returns to CSR. These findings distinguish broad CSR engagement from operational carbon outcomes and reinforce the role of carbon efficiency in sustainable airline strategy.

title: Contribution of Shri Guru Granth Sahib Ji in the Field of management and corporate governance: A conceptual study
summary: Today the organisations are becoming globalised and innovative, due to which stakeholders are seeking organisations to remain transparent, ethical and accountable. However, in today’s scenario, corporate scandals and ethical failures are increasing day by day, which creates a fundamental gap in contemporary management, resulting in absence of spiritual and value- based frameworks. When the religious scriptures are examined through contemporary lens, they offer a timeless wisdom that guides sustainable and ethical governance. Among these, Shri Guru Granth Sahib ji (SGGS), the eternal Guru of Sikhs, stands out to be not only a religious text but also a detailed guide to life management, leadership and governance. Truth ( Sat ), humility ( Nimrata ), justice ( Nyaya ) and service ( seva ) are the teachings from Shri Guru Granth Sahib which connects profoundly with the principles of corporate governance, human resource management, leadership ethics, and corporate social responsibility (CSR). This paper is a conceptual based research paper supported by secondary literature, to demonstrate the importance of SGGS in contemporary business. The concepts from SGGS such as Kirat Karni (honest living), Vand Chakna (sharing with others), and Sach Achar (truthful conduct) are connected with various management theories like stakeholder engagement, transformational leadership and sustainability to highlight that how the ancient wisdom can shape modern business practices. Through this study, a research gap is addressed where the teachings of the SGGS have not been sufficiently integrated with established management frameworks like the OECD governance principles. In the end, this paper concludes that adopting a Gurbani based framework enables a better balance between profit and the needs of people, a higher purpose, and the planet.

title: Pengaruh Digitalisasi Sistem Informasi Akuntansi dan Transparansi Informasi Keuangan terhadap Minat Investasi dengan Persepsi Nasabah sebagai Variabel Mediasi
summary: The rapid development of digital technology has encouraged financial institutions to implement digital-based accounting information systems and enhance financial information transparency to improve service quality for customers. As one of Indonesia’s non-bank financial institutions, PT Pegadaian has implemented digital transformation through the Pegadaian Digital (Tring!) application, which facilitates customers in conducting various gold investment transactions. However, the convenience offered by digital services does not necessarily lead to an increase in customers’ investment interest. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the effect of Accounting Information System Digitalization and Financial Information Transparency on Investment Interest, with Customer Perception serving as a mediating variable at PT Pegadaian Sukabumi Branch. This study employed a quantitative approach using a survey method involving 89 customers of PT Pegadaian Sukabumi Branch who use the Pegadaian Digital (Tring!) application. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4 software. The results indicate that Accounting Information System Digitalization has no significant effect on either Customer Perception or Investment Interest. In contrast, Financial Information Transparency has a positive and significant effect on both Customer Perception and Investment Interest. Furthermore, Customer Perception has a positive and significant effect on Investment Interest. The mediation analysis reveals that Customer Perception does not mediate the relationship between Accounting Information System Digitalization and Investment Interest, but it partially mediates the relationship between Financial Information Transparency and Investment Interest. These findings indicate that Financial Information Transparency plays a more dominant role than Accounting Information System Digitalization in enhancing customers’ investment interest.

title: Pengaruh Profitabilitas, Solvabilitas, dan Cost to Sales Ratio terhadap Manajemen Laba pada Perusahaan Sektor Industrial di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: This study examines the effect of profitability (ROE), solvency (DAR), and Cost to sales ratio on earnings management in industrial companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (2020–2024). Using purposive sampling , 38 companies (190 firm-year observations) were analyzed via panel data regression (EViews 12), with earnings management measured using the Stubben (2010) discretionary revenue model and a dummy variable controlling three outlier observations. Results show profitability, solvency, and Cost to sales ratio do not partially affect earnings management (prob. 0.4097; 0.5181; 0.8114; p > 0.05), but jointly affect it significantly (F = 7.189892; prob. 0.000021; p < 0.05). Adjusted R-squared of 11.58% indicates most variation is explained by factors outside the model, such as corporate governance, audit quality, and firm size. Findings suggest earnings management during the post-pandemic recovery is driven by combined financial characteristics rather than a single indicator, contributing new evidence on cost efficiency (Cost to sales ratio) as an underexplored factor in earnings management research.

title: Does supply chain digitalization affect corporate tax avoidance?
summary: Purpose The impact of supply chain digitization on corporate tax avoidance is a critical yet under-explored issue in tax governance within the digital economy. Against this backdrop, this paper aims to conduct an in-depth analysis of the underlying mechanisms and boundary conditions governing the relationship between the two. Design/methodology/approach This paper uses data from Chinese A-share listed companies (2011–2022) and uses a two-way fixed-effects model to test for direct effects, as well as conducting robustness tests, mediation tests, moderation tests and heterogeneity tests. Findings Supply chain digitalization significantly inhibits corporate tax avoidance, and the alleviation of financing constraints exerts a positive mediating effect in this relationship. Public scrutiny reinforces this curbing effect, while management myopia weakens it. Furthermore, this effect exhibits significant heterogeneity across different firms. In terms of economic consequences, the curbing effect of supply chain digitization on tax avoidance further reduces corporates’ risk-taking and enhances their reputation. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this paper provides the first empirical evidence that supply chain digitalization curbs corporate tax avoidance. By examining moderating effects and heterogeneous roles, and by linking the reduction in corporate tax avoidance to subsequent risk-taking and reputational outcomes, this paper further extends the boundaries of the literature in relevant fields. These findings offer several policy implications.

title: Financial Reporting Completeness and the Quality of Audit Reports: Evidence from Kenyan Public Universities
summary: Financial reporting completeness is critical to the credibility of financial information and the effectiveness of external auditing in public institutions. In Kenyan public universities, weaknesses in the completeness of financial statements, disclosures, supporting documentation, and reporting of financial obligations may affect audit report quality. This study evaluated the influence of financial reporting completeness on audit report quality in Kenyan public universities. The study was guided by Agency Theory and adopted a positivist research philosophy and cross-sectional research design. The target population comprised 175 respondents drawn from 35 publicly chartered universities in Kenya, including Deputy Vice Chancellors (Finance and Administration), Chief Finance Officers, internal auditors, accountants, and members of audit or finance committees. The study used a census approach at the institutional level, while purposive sampling selected respondents with direct knowledge of financial reporting and audit processes. The study collected primary data using structured questionnaires and obtained secondary data from published financial statements and audit reports. A pilot study involving 40 respondents from four public chartered universities achieved a 100% response rate. Reliability analysis established Cronbach?s alpha coefficients of 0.886 for financial reporting completeness and 0.914 for audit report quality, confirming satisfactory internal consistency. Data from 151 respondents, representing an 86.3% response rate, were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression. Descriptive findings indicated that financial reporting completeness was practiced to a moderately high extent (M = 3.68, SD = 1.16). Pearson correlation analysis found a strong, positive, and statistically significant relationship between financial reporting completeness and audit report quality (r = .711, p < .001). Regression analysis further showed that financial reporting completeness significantly predicted audit report quality, explaining 50.6% of its variation (R? = .506, adjusted R? = .503). The regression model was statistically significant, F (1,149) = 152.33, p < .001, while financial reporting completeness had a positive and statistically significant effect on audit report quality (B = .295, ? = .711, t = 12.366, p < .001). The null hypothesis was therefore rejected. The study concludes that greater completeness of financial reporting is associated with higher-quality audit reports. Public universities should strengthen financial reporting completeness, particularly in disclosing contingent liabilities, potential financial obligations, and future financial risks, alongside stronger pre-audit financial reporting reviews.

title: Supply Chain Sustainability Disclosure and Firm Performance: Evidence from Saudi Listed Firms
summary: The objective of this research is to find out if supply chain sustainability disclosure is related to firm performance among publicly traded companies in Saudi Arabia. A unique and valid Supply Chain Sustainability Disclosure Index (SCDI) that has six variables is measured based on the standards in the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) (2019) which are GRI 204, GRI 308, and GRI 414 through a systematic content analysis of 142 annual accounts of 58 publicly-listed non-financial corporations on the Saudi stock exchange (Tadawul) from 2022 to 2025. This study uses several panel regressions with fixed effects with respect to firm and year while using clustered standard errors of classified at the firm level. The study did not discover any evidence of a statistically significant connection between disclosure rates of the Supply Chain Sustainability Disclosure Index (SCDI) and firm performance measured by Return on Assets (ROA) or Return on Equity (ROE) taking into consideration various models such as main, lagged, ESG- alternative and restricted samples of the gathered data. The findings illustrate that the SCDI was found to be 0.11 while it had a median value of zero which indicates very little disclosure of Supply Chain sustainability. Therefore, it was concluded that in this window of opportunity and market, disclosure is mostly linked to the process of legitimation rather than performance-based signaling, due to the lack of variation among the gathered sample.

title: Axiology of Basic Education in the Land of Batak: Tension Between Traditional Values of Hamoraon, Hagabeon, Hasangapon And Modernization
summary: Basic education in Batak Land has long been driven by three cultural values: Hamoraon (prosperity), Hagabeon (descendants), and Hasangapon (honor). Modernization now challenges this value system through individual aspirations, a digital economy, language shift, and weakening communal social control. This study aims to describe how the three values operate as an axiological system in basic education, to identify the tensions that modernization produces, and to formulate a model of axiological reconciliation. A qualitative library research design was used. The corpus consisted of 33 documents published between 2018 and 2026, screened against explicit criteria and analyzed through content analysis with thematic coding. The results show four strands of literature: meaning and practice of Batak values (8 documents), axiological framing (6), integration of local wisdom into curriculum (11), and modernization pressures (8). One document reports that only 30% of Batak Toba adolescents aged 15 to 18 in a Medan district maintain the language, and another reports 17 million Indonesians identifying as content creators. None of the six axiological documents was situated in a Batak community. The study concludes that the tension is a problem of interpretation and transmission rather than a clash of rival value systems. A reconciliation model combining reinterpretation of the values, curricular embedding, and community partnership is proposed, with mother-tongue value vocabulary as an enabling condition. Implications are discussed for curriculum design, teacher education, and regional education policy.

title: Corporate Transparency and Disclosure Obligations in India
summary: Efficient disclosure methods ensure that investors obtain precise, prompt and thorough information about the financial status, governance framework and operational activities of companies. In India, corporate transparency and disclosure obligations secure accountability through mandatory reporting under the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. These rules promote investor trust by requiring timely financial statements, annual reporting, a governance framework and ESG disclosures. This paper examines the legal provisions governing corporate disclosure in India under the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and assesses the role of the Securities and Exchange Board of India in promoting transparency and safeguarding investors. It offers an examination of investor protection, corporate responsibility and transparency in the Indian capital markets, analyses the extent to which corporate disclosure practices protect investors' interests and enhance market transparency, and identifies issues and gaps in the existing disclosure system. The research also examines the effects of insufficient disclosure on investor trust.

title: Digital Transformation in Commerce & Business Management: Emerging Trends and Future Prospects
summary: Digital transformation has emerged as a fundamental driver of change in commerce and business management, reshaping how organisations operate, compete, and create value. The integration of technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data analytics, blockchain, Internet of Things, automation, and digital payment systems has transformed traditional business models and consumer interactions. This paper examines the emerging trends in digital transformation and evaluates their implications for commerce and business management. It focuses on the increasing adoption of e-commerce, data-driven decision-making, intelligent automation, personalised customer experiences, digital supply chains, and platform-based business models. The study also considers challenges related to cybersecurity, data privacy, digital skills, technological costs, and organisational resistance to change. Further, it explores future prospects associated with artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, immersive technologies, and sustainable digital business practices. The paper highlights the need for organisations to develop adaptive strategies, technological capabilities, and digitally skilled human resources to achieve sustainable growth in an increasingly technology-driven business environment

title: Big Data Analytics and Contemporary Accounting
summary: This paper examines big data analytics and contemporary accounting from conceptual, practical and contemporary perspectives. The study discusses the development of the subject, major accounting practices, its contribution to organisational decision-making, technological changes, professional challenges and future directions. Accounting is increasingly understood as an information-based discipline that connects financial reporting with management, governance, risk assessment and stakeholder accountability. The paper adopts a conceptual approach and draws on established accounting literature and professional standards. It highlights the importance of reliable financial information, effective internal controls, ethical professional conduct and appropriate use of technology. The discussion also recognises that accounting practices are influenced by organisational circumstances, regulatory requirements and changes in the wider business environment. The paper concludes that the continuing relevance of accounting depends on its capacity to provide useful, credible and timely information while adapting to digital transformation and emerging expectations concerning transparency and accountability.

title: Corporate ownership and the effectiveness of management accounting tools in enhancing ESG performance
summary: This research explores how management accounting instruments, Balanced Scorecard (BSC), Benchmarking, and Environmental Management Accounting (EMA), affect ESG performance in publicly-traded food firms in Asia between 2019 and 2023. With panel data of 51 companies, and fixed effects regression, the study concludes that BSC and EMA have a significant positive effect on ESG performance, which emphasizes their strategic importance in incorporating sustainability into corporate decision making. There is no notable impact of benchmarking, indicating that ESG alignment is not very great in practice. The negative correlation between profitability and ESG performance implies the potential short-term trade-offs in investments in sustainability. Moreover, the corporate ownership also has a positive moderating role in the connection between accounting tools and ESG results, indicating that the governance structure promotes the effectiveness of ESG. The results provide practical implications to companies that need to enhance sustainability performance and add to the body of knowledge in strategic accounting and integration of ESG.

title: OFF-BUDGET FINANCING, CENTRAL BANK MANDATES, AND LONG-TERM INVESTMENT MOBILIZATION IN INDONESIA
summary: In recent years, the increasing emphasis on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues has transformed the way companies communicate their performance and long-term sustainability. This study aims to examine the impact of ESG disclosure and sustainability accounting practices on firm value in the context of Indonesian listed companies. By integrating the concept of transparency and stakeholder trust, this research explores whether more comprehensive ESG reporting contributes to enhanced market valuation and investor confidence. This study employs a quantitative research approach using secondary data collected from annual reports and sustainability reports of publicly listed companies in Indonesia. ESG disclosure is measured using a disclosure index based on widely recognized reporting standards, while sustainability accounting practices are proxied through the extent of environmental and social cost recognition. Firm value is measured using indicators such as Tobin’s Q and market-to-book ratio. The data are analyzed using multiple regression techniques to assess the relationship between variables. The findings are expected to demonstrate that higher levels of ESG disclosure and more robust sustainability accounting practices positively influence firm value. Companies that provide transparent and comprehensive ESG information are more likely to gain investor trust, reduce information asymmetry, and strengthen their reputation in the capital market. Furthermore, sustainability accounting practices are anticipated to reinforce the credibility of ESG disclosures by providing measurable and accountable financial information related to sustainability activities. This research contributes to the growing body of literature on sustainability reporting and corporate value, particularly in emerging markets like Indonesia. It also provides practical implications for corporate managers, regulators, and investors by highlighting the importance of integrating ESG considerations into financial reporting frameworks. Ultimately, this study underscores the role of transparency in building trust, which in turn enhances firm value and supports sustainable economic development.

title: Implementasi Good Governance dalam Pengelolaan Keuangan Daerah pada Badan Keuangan dan Aset Daerah (BKAD) Kota Kupang
summary: This study examines regional financial management at the Regional Financial and Asset Management Agency (BKAD) of Kupang City and evaluates the implementation of good governance principles. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, with data collected through interviews, observations, and document analysis. Data were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman method, consisting of data collection, data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification. The findings indicate that BKAD Kupang City manages regional finances in accordance with Government Regulation (PP) Number 12 of 2019 and Minister of Home Affairs Regulation (Permendagri) Number 77 of 2020. Financial management covers planning, budgeting, execution, administration, reporting, accountability, and oversight. Good governance principles are generally well implemented. Transparency is supported by financial information disclosure and the Regional Government Information System (SIPD), while accountability is reflected in financial reporting. Participation is facilitated through the Development Planning Deliberation (Musrenbang), and effectiveness and efficiency are supported by information systems and coordination among regional government units. Compliance with regulations also demonstrates the implementation of the rule of law. However, challenges include delays in data submission, limited human resource capacity in responding to regulatory changes, and the need to adapt to evolving information systems. Overall, good governance implementation supports transparent, accountable, effective, efficient, and compliant regional financial management.

title: Pengaruh Kualitas Audit, Komite Audit, dan Ukuran Perusahaan terhadap Integritas Laporan Keuangan
summary: This research aims to examine the effect of audit quality, audit committee, and firm size on financial reporting integrity in energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2020–2024 period. The population consisted of 91 energy sector companies listed on the IDX as of 2024. The sample was selected using a purposive sampling technique, resulting in 51 companies that met the predetermined criteria. Data processing was conducted using Microsoft Excel 2019, while the empirical analysis employed panel data regression using EViews 12. The results indicate that audit quality, audit committee, and firm size simultaneously affect financial reporting integrity. Partially, audit quality has a significant effect on financial reporting integrity, whereas the audit committee and firm size do not have a significant effect on financial reporting integrity. The results of this study demonstrate the importance of audit quality in supporting the integrity of financial reporting in energy sector companies. These findings can be used as a basis for companies to improve their monitoring and reporting mechanisms to maintain the quality and integrity of financial information.

title: Accounting Information System Understanding and Student Financial Reporting Quality: Human Resource Quality as Moderator
summary: This study examined the effects of Accounting Information System (AIS) understanding and human resource quality on students’ financial reporting quality and tested the moderating role of human resource quality. An explanatory cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 150 accounting department students at Universitas Cenderawasih who had completed AIS coursework. Purposive sampling was applied and the data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). AIS understanding positively affected financial reporting quality (β=0.482, t=8.063, p<0.001), as did human resource quality (β=0.474, t=6.071, p<0.001). The interaction was not significant (β=0.009, t=0.232, p=0.817, f²=0.0004). The model explained 75.7% of the variance and showed positive predictive relevance. AIS understanding and human resource quality operated mainly as parallel direct capabilities rather than complementary moderators. The single-institution, cross-sectional design and the single-indicator final AIS construct limited generalizability and measurement breadth. The study extends AIS and reporting-quality research to accounting education in Papua and clarifies the boundary of competence-based moderation.

title: Impact of AI Adoption on Profitability: A Comparative Study of Leading Indian Public Online Travel Agencies
summary: Abstract: This study examines the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption on the profitability of two leading Indian online travel agencies (OTAs), IRCTC and EasyMyTrip (EMT). Using a longitudinal descriptive-comparative research design, secondary financial data covering three years before and after AI adoption were analysed. Paired sample t-tests and trend analysis were employed to evaluate changes in net profit following AI implementation. The findings indicate that EasyMyTrip experienced a statistically significant improvement in profitability after AI adoption, reflecting the benefits of strategic digital transformation and business expansion. In contrast, IRCTC recorded a positive but statistically insignificant increase in profitability, largely influenced by external factors such as the COVID-19 pandemic and operational constraints. The study highlights the role of AI in enhancing organisational performance and provides practical insights for tourism enterprises, policymakers, and researchers on leveraging AI for sustainable financial growth. title: Risk Governance and Quality of Financial Reporting Among Commercial State-Owned Entities in Kenya
summary: The reliability of financial reports underpins accountability and service delivery in State-Owned Commercial Entities (SOCEs), yet weak board-level oversight, political interference, and recurrent audit qualifications continue to undermine credibility in Kenya. This paper reports one component of a larger doctoral study on Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) and financial reporting quality; it examines the effect of risk governance, the first of the four ERM dimensions investigated in that study, on the quality of financial reporting among commercial State-Owned Entities in Kenya. Risk governance is examined on its own because it is the structural layer within which the remaining dimensions operate. The study was anchored on Agency Theory and adopted an explanatory research design within a positivist research philosophy. A multi-stage probability sampling procedure was used: commercial SOCEs were first sampled as clusters, respondents within the sampled entities were then stratified by professional category, and participants were selected within each stratum by simple random sampling. Applying the Yamane (1967) formula to a target population of 420 finance, audit, risk, and legal personnel yielded a sample of 205, of whom 160 returned complete and usable questionnaires, a response rate of 78.0%. Content validity was established through expert review, and reliability was assessed using Cronbach’s Alpha, with the Risk Governance construct achieving a coefficient of 0.836 and the Financial Reporting Quality construct. Both constructs were measured perceptually on a five-point Likert scale. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression in SPSS Version 27. Risk governance had a positive and statistically significant association with the quality of financial reporting (B = 0.668, 95% CI [0.571, 0.765], R² = 0.540, F(1, 158) = 185.15, t = 13.607, p < .001, Cohen’s f² = 1.17), leading to rejection of the null hypothesis. Risk governance was also positively and significantly correlated with financial reporting quality (r = 0.735, 95% CI [0.654, 0.799], p < .01). The study concludes that risk governance is strongly associated with financial reporting quality among commercial SOCEs in Kenya, with board-level risk oversight structures, risk mapping, and independent assurance mechanisms being the practices most closely linked to reporting quality. The study recommends that the National Treasury and the State Corporations Advisory Committee prioritise strengthening board-level risk governance structures across all commercial SOCEs, including regular review of risk governance frameworks and clearer independent assurance mechanisms through internal audit and external review. The findings are useful to policymakers, SOCE boards and management, oversight institutions, and scholars seeking to strengthen public sector accountability and risk management practice in Kenya.

title: Optimalisasi Investasi Wakaf Uang melalui Diversifikasi Aset dan Peningkatan Kapasitas Nazhir: Studi Kasus Badan Wakaf Uang Muhammadiyah Sumatera Barat
summary: Aims: This study aims to analyze the optimization of waqf investment at Badan Wakaf Uang Muhammadiyah (BWUM) West Sumatra by focusing on waqf asset diversification, investment management, risk control, and the utilization of investment returns for community welfare. Method: This research employs a qualitative approach using an ex-post facto method. Data were collected through interviews and documentation related to waqf investment management at BWUM West Sumatra. The data were analyzed descriptively to examine the practices of investment development, supervision, reporting, risk management, and distribution of waqf benefits. Results: The findings indicate that BWUM West Sumatra has developed waqf funds through Islamic financial institutions and productive business activities, including UD Berkah. However, several investments have been discontinued due to considerations of efficiency and sustainability. Waqf investment management is supported by supervision, financial reporting, reserve fund establishment, and the distribution of investment benefits to social, educational, and healthcare sectors. These findings demonstrate that waqf investment optimization requires a balance between asset development, risk control, professional nazhir management, transparency, and the orientation toward public welfare. Conclusion/Novelty/Implications: The novelty of this study lies in its integrated analysis of waqf investment optimization by linking asset diversification, investment management, risk control, and the utilization of investment returns within the context of BWUM West Sumatra. The findings imply that strengthening nazhir professionalism, investment governance, transparency, and risk management is essential to ensure the sustainability and productivity of waqf assets. Future efforts should emphasize broader asset diversification, more strategic investment planning, and the development of productive waqf models that generate sustainable socio-economic benefits for the community.

title: INTEGRATION OF MICRO AND SMALL ENTERPRISES INTO E-COMMERCE: A STUDY APPLIED TO THE CONTEXT OF THE ALI PRODUCTIVITY PROGRAM
summary: This study analyzes the strategies adopted by Brazilian micro and small enterprises (MSEs) in the use of marketplaces as sales channels in electronic commerce, with a focus on initiatives developed within the Brasil Mais Produtividade Program through the work of the Local Innovation Agent (ALI). It is a qualitative, applied research project, with data collected from six MSEs in the municipality of São Bento do Sul, Santa Catarina, representing different economic sectors. The methodology included a diagnostic assessment using the Innovation Radar, SWOT analysis, the “5 Whys” technique, and the 5W2H framework, in addition to continuous monitoring over six months. The results show that the adoption of practices such as search engine optimization (SEO), strengthening brand identity, and personalized customer‑relationship strategies were decisive for increasing visibility and performance in marketplaces. The practical experience highlights the role of the ALI as a facilitator of innovative solutions adapted to the reality of MSEs, contributing to their digital transformation and greater competitiveness in e‑commerce. The originality of this study lies in its empirical approach to applying innovation‑management tools (such as the Innovation Radar, SWOT, 5 Whys, and 5W2H) to the real context of micro and small enterprises, examining their outcomes within the practical intervention framework of SEBRAE's ALI Productivity Program.

title: Praktik Akuntansi Kompensasi Tenaga Kerja Berbasis PSAK 24 pada Rumah Sakit Syariah
summary: Employee compensation is a form of employee entitlement that requires proper accounting treatment so that the organization’s obligations can be recognized, measured, and reported in accordance with standards. This study aims to analyze employee compensation accounting practices at Sharia hospitals based on Financial Accounting Standards Board (PSAK) Statement No. 24 on employee benefits. This study employs a qualitative method with a descriptive approach. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and document review involving informants from the finance, human resources, and health and non-health care staff departments. Data were analyzed through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions. Data validity was tested through source and technique triangulation. The results show that employee compensation practices are implemented through a remuneration system that considers corporate grade, ten remuneration weighting factors, Individual Performance Indicators (IKI), and Key Hospital Performance Indicators (KPH). Compensation is recognized as an expense and liability at the end of the period. Compensation measurement is based on the remuneration system and performance indicators implemented by the hospital. In terms of reporting, unpaid compensation liabilities are recorded as operating liabilities. Recognition and measurement practices are generally in accordance with PSAK 24, particularly for short-term employee benefits, whereas the application of long-term employee benefits, as well as reporting and disclosure, still need to be optimized. This study highlights the importance of improving consistency in the application of PSAK 24 in the management and reporting of employee compensation at Sharia hospitals.

title: Heterogeneous effects of bottom-up responsiveness and top-down central environmental inspection on corporate green innovation across ownership and competition
summary: This paper examines how bottom-up municipal responsiveness and top-down central environmental inspection pressure shape firms' green innovation behavior in China. Using a firm-level panel of all non-financial A-listed firms, patent data from the China Research Data Services Platform, a city-level government responsiveness index, and the first round of Central Environmental Protection Inspections, we study how different environmental governance pressures are associated with green innovation in firms’ overall innovation portfolios. To address endogeneity in municipal responsiveness, we use an instrumental-variable strategy based on lagged leave-one-out responsiveness of other cities within the same province. To examine central inspection pressure, we combine province-cohort exposure regressions with double/debiased machine learning, recognizing that all provinces were eventually inspected and that the design therefore lacks a conventional never-treated control group. The results are consistent with a dual-channel pattern. Municipal responsiveness is positively associated with firms' green innovation share mainly in the contemporaneous specification and among non-SOEs (state-owned enterprises), consistent with a bottom-up local governance-signaling mechanism. By contrast, central inspection exposure is associated with a stronger green innovation response among SOEs, consistent with a top-down political accountability mechanism. For non-SOEs, market competition weakens the conversion of central inspection exposure into green innovation. These findings suggest that environmental governance does not affect firms’ innovation behavior uniformly: its association with green innovation depends on the level of government from which pressure originates, the ownership structure of the firm, and the competitive environment in which the firm operates.

title: Managing supplier risk through procurement decisions: a decision-making framework for the automotive industry
summary: Purpose Automotive supply chains face increasing exposure to supplier-related disruptions, yet existing frameworks inadequately integrate risk categorisation, procurement decision-making, and supply chain resilience into a unified decision-support structure. This study addresses that challenge by developing and validating a theory-grounded supplier risk decision-making framework for procurement managers in the automotive industry. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review (SLR) of peer-reviewed publications was conducted to synthesise supplier risk typologies and procurement decision frameworks. The resulting framework was subsequently validated through structured interviews with automotive industry experts to ensure practical applicability and managerial relevance. Findings This study presents a comprehensive supplier risk categorisation comprising six major risk types and thirty-seven contributing factors. Procurement decisions are organised into three groups: supplier categorisation, supplier performance management, and supplier relationship management. A novel supplier risk decision-making framework, grounded in prescriptive decision theory and informed by contingency theory, delineates strategic, tactical and operational decision-making stages to support effective supplier risk mitigation. Practical implications The framework has been adopted by a leading UK automotive manufacturer to train procurement professionals, providing evidence of its practical relevance and real-world applicability. Social implications The framework contributes to more stable and resilient automotive supply chains, supporting business continuity and reducing the broader economic disruptions associated with supplier failures in a sector of considerable economic importance. Originality/value The proposed framework integrates supplier risk management, supply chain resilience and procurement decisions, offering a holistic foundation for effective and informed decision-making.

title: Sustainability Reporting as a Catalyst: How ESG Performance Shapes Corporate Financial Outcomes in Taiwan
summary: ABSTRACT How sustainability information enters managerial and market decision‐making remains an open question. While firms increasingly invest in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) activities, capital markets can price such performance only when it is observable, comparable, and credible. This study examines whether sustainability reporting serves as an information‐economic mechanism that enables ESG performance to translate into corporate financial outcomes. Using the TESG index, the first SASB‐authorized ESG database in Taiwan, this study evaluates key financial indicators including ROA, ROE, and Tobin's Q to assess how ESG practices translate into measurable outcomes. The empirical findings reveal that firms with stronger ESG performance tend to exhibit superior financial results. In addition, the formal disclosure of sustainability reports is shown to be a significant moderating factor, strengthening the linkage between ESG efforts and financial value creation. These results provide strategic insights for firms navigating the global “Net Zero” transition and highlight the critical role of transparent sustainability disclosure in enhancing market confidence and supporting informed decision‐making in capital markets.

title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON THE PLANNING IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative catalyst in Supply Chain Management (SCM), shifting operations from traditional models to predictive and automated systems. This article examines the impact of AI technologies—specifically Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), on supply chain planning. Grounded in Organizational Information Processing Theory (OIPT) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory (DCT), we analyze how AI enhances planning efficiency across strategic, tactical, and operational horizons. Furthermore, we critically evaluate key implementation challenges, including data governance, system integration, algorithmic transparency, human-AI trust, and organizational change management. The article concludes with key managerial insights and future research directions for sustainable, resilient, and AI-augmented supply chains.

title: Local creative culture environment and corporate digital transformation: evidence from cultural and creative industry parks in China
summary: Based on a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we investigate the influence of the local creative culture environment on corporate digital transformation (DT). The results show that a vibrant creative culture environment is positively related to firms’ DT, primarily through three channels: higher R&D investments, lower financing constraints and higher regional digital talent agglomeration. Moreover, heterogeneity analyses reveal that this effect is more pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises, in regions with weaker Confucian cultural traditions, and in firms with a higher proportion of female executives. We enhance the literature on the drivers of DT from the perspective of the local creative culture environment. The findings also provide policy implications for promoting the synergies between cultural development and the digital economy.

title: Climate Finance and State Capacity in Africa: Institutional Constraints on Climate-Policy Implementation
summary: The financing of climate change in Africa has become the focus of climate change policy implementation, since most African nations have significant adaptation and mitigation needs and are experiencing low-carbon development, and are constrained by limited fiscal resources. However, access to finance is not enough to ensure good policy implementation. This article explores the linkage between climate finance and state capacity in Africa, detailing the constraints that shape a State's capacity to mobilise, access, allocate, execute, monitor and account for climate-related financial resources. The article concludes that Africa's climate policy implementation issue is a financing issue and a state capacity issue, based on evidence compiled from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), the African Development Bank (AfDB), the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank, Climate Policy Institute (CPI), the OECD and recent peer-reviewed research. African countries are also burdened with challenges on how to prepare projects, public financial management, intergovernmental coordination, data systems, institutional mandates, monitoring and evaluation, and fiduciary and technical needs of international climate funds. Experience in Ghana, Uganda, Nigeria, Kenya, Rwanda, and Africa in general has shown that the establishment of a formal climate plan and legislation often outpaces the institutional structures and processes needed to execute it. The article instead theorises the climate finance as a tool for governance that is only effective in its development according to how well the institution can absorb it. It finds that scaling up climate finance in Africa needs to be accompanied by a simultaneous reform of domestic fiscal systems, the process of project preparation, climate budgeting, public investment management, coordination, subnational capacity, monitoring, and direct access to international climate funds.

title: Pengaruh Profitabilitas, Likuiditas dan Audit Tenure terhadap Opini Audit Going Concern
summary: Transportation and logistics companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) provide services in the fields of transportation and supply chain management. To provide stakeholders with a clear picture of their internal condition for future decision-making, these business entities are required to publish audited financial statements. This study examines the influence of profitability, liquidity, and audit tenure on the issuance of going-concern audit opinions for companies in the transportation and logistics sector. A quantitative approach was employed, covering a population of 38 transportation and logistics companies over the 2021–2024 period. Using purposive sampling, 28 companies were selected for a four-year observation period, resulting in a final sample of 112 observations. The study relies on secondary data-specifically audited annual reports—obtained directly from the companies or the IDX. Data processing was conducted using logistic regression analysis via SPSS software (version 26). The findings indicate that profitability, liquidity, and audit tenure do not have a significant influence on going-concern audit opinions.

title: Geopolitical Competition in the Arctic and Its Impact on Indo-Pacific Security
summary: The Arctic has rapidly emerged as a critical arena of geopolitical competition owing to accelerating climate change, melting sea ice, expanding access to natural resources, and the opening of new maritime routes. Once viewed primarily as a region of scientific cooperation and environmental governance, the Arctic is increasingly becoming a theatre of strategic rivalry among major powers, including Russia, the United States, China, and NATO members. This transformation extends beyond the Arctic itself, generating significant implications for the Indo-Pacific, where maritime security, trade, energy flows, and strategic competition are already intensifying. This article examines the evolving geopolitical dynamics in the Arctic and analyses their impact on Indo-Pacific security within the broader framework of contemporary global power politics. It explores the strategic significance of emerging Arctic shipping routes, competition over critical minerals and hydrocarbons, military modernization, China's "Polar Silk Road," Russia's Arctic strategy, and the responses of Indo-Pacific stakeholders such as India, Japan, Australia, and the United States. The study argues that developments in the Arctic are increasingly interconnected with Indo-Pacific security through maritime trade, supply chain resilience, technological competition, climate governance, and the evolving balance of power. It concludes that strengthening international cooperation, promoting sustainable governance, and enhancing cross-regional strategic dialogue will be essential to maintaining stability across both regions in an era of intensifying geopolitical competition.

title: Pengaruh Pergantian Auditor, Kepemilikan Institusional, dan Audit Fee terhadap Audit Delay
summary: Timely audited financial reporting is important for investors and other stakeholders, yet audit delay remains a concern among listed companies, including those in the property and real estate sector. This study examines the effect of auditor switching, institutional ownership, and audit fee on audit delay in property and real estate companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2019–2024. The study employed a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from annual reports and financial statements. Using purposive sampling, 33 companies were selected, resulting in 198 firm-year observations. The data were analyzed using panel data regression with EViews 12. The findings indicate that auditor switching and audit fee significantly affect audit delay, while institutional ownership does not have a significant effect. Simultaneously, auditor switching, institutional ownership, and audit fee significantly affect audit delay. These findings indicate that changes in auditors and audit fee are relevant factors in understanding variations in audit completion time, whereas institutional ownership alone does not appear sufficient to determine audit delay in the observed companies.

title: Linking Perceived Corporate Social Responsibility to Brand Loyalty and Brand Advocacy Intention: Brand Trust and Value Co-Creation in Hotel Customer Relationships
summary: This study examines how hotel customers’ perceptions of corporate social responsibility (CSR) are associated with brand loyalty and brand advocacy intention through brand trust and value co-creation. Drawing on signaling theory, relationship-based social exchange reasoning, and service-dominant logic, survey data collected from 638 hotel customers recruited in Taiwan between May and June 2026 were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Perceived CSR was positively associated with brand trust; brand trust was positively associated with value co-creation; and both brand trust and value co-creation were positively associated with loyalty and advocacy intention. The direct CSR–outcome associations were not significant, whereas the proposed indirect associations were significant. Competing-model analyses qualified the serial interpretation: a parallel model remained plausible, and a partial sequential model showed significant CSR–VCC and BT–VCC paths, indicating that trust is a meaningful but not exclusive pathway to participation. Supplementary measurement analyses supported an overarching value co-creation representation while confirming borderline first-order convergent validity. The findings concern customer–brand relationship associations rather than sustainability-specific behavior or hotel sustainability performance. Managerially, hotels should emphasize credible CSR communication and accessible opportunities for customer participation rather than assuming that favorable CSR perceptions directly translate into loyalty or advocacy.

title: Shareholder Activism and Corporate Governance: A Comparative Study of India, the United Kingdom and the United States
summary: Shareholder activism has emerged as one of the most potent forces shaping the landscape of corporate governance throughout the world. What started out as a peripheral concern of corporate law thirty years ago has burgeoned into the primary means through which owners of capital seek to 'discipline management', 'control strategy' and 'challenge the board'. The manifestation, intensity and treatment of activism, however, vary profoundly depending on how corporate ownership is organised, the provisions of a jurisdiction's securities law regime, and whether its courts are prepared to intervene in disputes within corporations. The paper offers a comparative overview of activism and corporate governance in three jurisdictions that embody clearly distinct governance traditions: (i) the United States, with a largely dispersed pattern of ownership and a landscape dominated by hedge funds engaged in aggressive activism; (ii) the United Kingdom, with a maturing, stewardship-centred soft law regime; and (iii) India, an economy of tightly concentrated, promoter-dominated companies in which activism remains nascent. Drawing on legislation, judicial decisions, regulatory reports and the extensive scholarly literature on the subject, the paper seeks to demonstrate that the success of an activist intervention depends less on rights that exist on paper than on the combination of the degree of concentration of shareholdings, the enforcement framework and the robustness of the institutional shareholder base. It concludes with proposals that the Indian system could draw, selectively and with caution, from the other two jurisdictions in order to make shareholder activism a more effective mechanism.

title: Toward Evidence‐Based ESG Reporting: The Added Value of Geospatial and Satellite Data
summary: ABSTRACT This study addresses the limitations of conventional ESG reporting, including reliance on self‐reported and third‐party data, lack of standardization, and limited verifiability, by examining how geospatial data enhance disclosure quality. It aims to synthesize and critically evaluate existing research on satellite and geospatial data in ESG reporting in order to identify dominant research directions and unresolved challenges. It employs a systematic bibliometric analysis of Scopus‐indexed publications, complemented by thematic mapping and cluster identification, to explore the structure and evolution of the literature. The findings demonstrate that geospatial data enhance environmental performance measurement, enable asset‐level monitoring, and strengthen risk assessment, thereby mitigating information asymmetries. Nevertheless, the diffusion of these data remains constrained by coverage gaps, methodological inconsistencies, and governance issues. Standardization and interoperability challenges can be tackled through stronger global governance and structured public‐private collaboration that aligns data production with concrete user needs in sustainable finance, agriculture, and environmental management.

title: CAPITAL STRUCTURE AND LIQUIDITY ON FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE: THE MODERATING ROLE OF GOOD CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
summary: The phenomenon of fluctuating financial performance in companies listed in the LQ45 index in Indonesia remains a concern, as indicated by changes in Net Profit Margin (NPM). This condition is influenced by internal factors such as capital structure, liquidity, and the implementation of good corporate governance that has not yet been optimal. This study aims to analyze the effect of capital structure and liquidity on financial performance with good corporate governance as a moderating variable. The data used are secondary data obtained from financial statements and annual reports of 20 LQ45 index companies during the 2022–2024 period. The analysis was conducted using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model (REM) through EViews 12. The results of this study indicate that capital structure and liquidity have a significant effect on financial performance. In addition, good corporate governance is able to moderate the effect of capital structure and liquidity on financial performance. The implications of this study emphasize the importance of optimal capital structure and liquidity management, as well as strengthening corporate governance to support the improvement of financial performance. This study is expected to serve as a consideration for company management and investors in making more effective and sustainable decisions.

title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance dan Investment Opportunity Set terhadap Kebijakan Dividen
summary: The increasing demand for transparent corporate governance and effective dividend policies has become a critical issue for companies operating in the mineral and coal sector, particularly due to the industry's capital-intensive nature and investment uncertainty. Understanding the factors that influence dividend policy is essential for balancing shareholders' expectations with corporate growth opportunities. This study aims to examine the effect of good corporate governance, proxied by managerial ownership and institutional ownership, and the investment opportunity set on dividend policy. This research employs an associative quantitative approach. The population consists of 23 mineral and coal sector companies listed during the observation period. The sample was selected using purposive sampling based on predetermined criteria, resulting in eight companies observed over five years, yielding a total of 40 panel data observations. Panel data regression analysis was applied to test the proposed hypotheses. The partial test results indicate that managerial ownership, as a proxy for good corporate governance, has no significant effect on dividend policy. In contrast, institutional ownership has a significant effect on dividend policy. The investment opportunity set also has a significant effect on dividend policy. Furthermore, the simultaneous test demonstrates that good corporate governance, represented by managerial ownership and institutional ownership, together with the investment opportunity set, significantly influences dividend policy. These findings provide empirical evidence regarding the determinants of dividend policy in the mineral and coal industry.

title: Development of integrated supply chains and digitalization of agricultural product sales channels
summary: The article provides a theoretical overview of the determinants of agri-food supply chain integration and develops a conceptual multi-level model for the digitalization of agricultural product sales channels. It shows that traditional linear distribution channels have exhausted their adaptive capacity amid geopolitical turbulence, climate risks, and rising transaction costs. To address the systemic exclusion of primary agricultural producers from value creation, the article proposes a transition to cyber-physical supply chains based on Industry 4.0 technologies. The article substantiates the economic impact of structural market disintermediation achieved through B2B agricultural exchanges, Short Food Supply Chain (SFSC) services, and logistics aggregators. The study outlines a synergistic technology stack: IoT sensors ensure continuous quality control and reduce physical raw material losses by 20–35%; blockchain and smart contracts optimize fund deposits via escrow, eliminating non-payment risk; and artificial intelligence algorithms enable predictive pricing and dynamic routing. The study finds that digitalizing sales channels reduces transaction costs by 15–25%, accelerates capital turnover by 4–8 times, cuts transport downtime by 40–50%, and increases selling prices for farmers by 7–15%. The paper focuses on Ukraine’s agricultural logistics under martial law, the redirection of export flows to Danube ports and western border crossings, and the role of the State Agrarian Registry (SAR) and the “eQueue” system in restoring export potential. A conceptual five-level model of the digital lifecycle of agricultural supply (“from field to settlement”) has been developed; this model minimizes the human factor, expands small businesses’ access to international markets, ensures transparent certification of grain batches, and lays the groundwork for the full integration of the domestic agricultural sector into the European Union’s single digital economic space. Keywords: agricultural logistics, supply chains, sales digitalization, Industry 4.0, smart contracts, blockchain, Internet of Things, B2B platforms.

title: Structural changes in the labor market under digital transformation
summary: The article examines the digital transformation of the Ukrainian labor market. It clarifies the concept by defining it as a systemic process of qualitative changes in the structure, functioning mechanisms, and interactions among labor market actors, driven by the adoption and diffusion of digital technologies. The study analyses how digital changes have been reflected in Ukraine’s strategic and regulatory documents. The study identifies a gradual broadening of the government’s approach to these issues, ranging from considering individual components of digital development to incorporating them comprehensively into national employment policy. This chapter synthesizes contemporary scholarly approaches to transformations in employment, work organization, occupational structure, regulatory mechanisms, and workforce requirements. The paper justifies systematizing digital changes in the labor market into six interrelated dimensions. The paper specifies the content of each dimension and shows that considering them together provides a comprehensive framework for characterizing government priorities for labor market development, regulatory mechanisms, the digital infrastructure that supports them, transformations in employment forms and occupational structure, and changing competency requirements for workers. The proposed systematization complements existing scholarly approaches to studying digital transformation in labor markets. It provides a theoretical foundation for identifying interrelationships among the distinguished dimensions, assessing the nature and intensity of the corresponding changes, and developing quantitative and qualitative indicators. The findings can support a comprehensive analysis of the labor market’s digital development, assess the nature and interrelationships of the identified changes, and identify priority areas for adaptation to technological transformations and evolving conditions of economic activity. Keywords: labor market, digital transformation, digital changes, digital development, employment, government regulation, digital infrastructure, occupational structure of employment, workforce competencies.

title: Segmenting Political Connection and Earnings Management: A Clustering and Regression Approach in IDX Firms
summary: This study aimed to segment 140 non-financial companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for fiscal year 2024 based on political connections and earnings management, and to test the consistency of this segmentation through Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression. Political connection was measured through five indicators, while earnings management was measured through discretionary accruals and two real-activities indicators, with normal-model coefficients estimated on a cross-section of 852 IDX-listed firms, Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and k-means clustering were then applied to the resulting factor scores, followed by ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis tests and OLS regression. Exploratory factor analysis yielded a robust two-factor structure (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin = 0.798, cumulative variance 72.6%), and k-means clustering produced a statistically optimal two-cluster solution (Silhouette = 0.616) that separated the sample purely by political connection, with no significant earnings-management difference (p>0.49), a three-cluster solution revealed one bootstrap-stable cluster with a significant income-increasing pattern (p<0.001). The findings were more consistent with the political shelter hypothesis than with political capture at the cluster profile and ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis levels, although a robustness check using clusters formed from the political-connection factor alone found no significant partial association, although the single-year cross-sectional design limited interpretation to association rather than causation. This study contributed methodologically by cross-validating the factor structure and complementing cluster segmentation with regression evidence.
