title: The Effect of Simulation-Based Internal Audit Engagements on Digital Competence and Professional Scepticism Among Auditing Students
summary: Digital transformation imperatives have resulted in many organisations migrating to digital spaces, to ensure they remain competitive. This has led to the shift of skills and competencies that are required from auditors. With this background, the study sought to assess the effects of simulation-based internal audit engagements on digital competence and professional scepticism among auditing students. This study is theoretically grounded in competence-based education (CBE). The study has employed mixed-research approach, questionnaire, student reflective journal and focused group interviews were used as a data collection tool. The data was collected form 98 students form a selected university that offers simulation-based auditing engagements. The study revealed that simulation-based internal audit engagements are an effective pedagogical strategy for preparing students for the modern auditing profession. The results further demonstrated that simulation-based auditing engagements significantly improves both digital competence and professional scepticism. These two competencies are increasingly recognised as essential for auditors operating in technologically complex environments. The study contributes to auditing education literature by providing empirical evidence supporting simulation-based pedagogies in developing future-ready internal auditors. The findings have implications for curriculum transformation, accreditation standards, and the integration of technology-enhanced learning within auditing programmes.

title: Impact-finance protocol for digital sustainable finance: institutional architecture for outcome-based capital allocation
summary: Introduction Modern financial systems are becoming increasingly digital, automated and data-driven. Yet the infrastructures linking trusted representations of real-world social and ecological performance to financial decision-making remain underdeveloped. This challenge is particularly acute within sustainable, impact and development finance, where capital allocation continues to rely heavily on retrospective reporting, proxy indicators and fragmented information flows. Methods This study addresses this gap through a design science approach, developing an Impact-Finance Protocol as a conceptual systems architecture for Digital Sustainable Finance. Drawing on systems mapping, comparative protocol analysis and the Integrated Capitals Assessment (ICA) framework, the research identifies the functional requirements for translating verified non-financial performance into adaptive financial processes. Results The resulting architecture comprises six interdependent protocol layers encompassing data, logic, value, governance, community and assessment. Together, these establish an integrated infrastructure through which verified impact information can inform financial decision-making, capital allocation and institutional governance within continuous feedback systems. Discussion Rather than proposing a new financial instrument, the protocol reconceptualises finance as an adaptive information system in which trusted digital infrastructure enables financial flows to respond dynamically to verified real-world conditions. The paper contributes a novel systems architecture for Digital Sustainable Finance and provides a conceptual foundation for future empirical research into blockchain-enabled, AI-enabled and other programmable financial infrastructures supporting sustainable, impact and development finance.

title: Influence of the Supply Chain Infrastructure Context on Procurement Policy Implementation among Insurance Companies in Kenya
summary: Purpose: This study examined the influence of the supply chain infrastructure context on procurement policy implementation among insurance companies in Kenya. Methodology: The study was grounded theoretically in Institutional Theory and adopted a descriptive cross-sectional survey research design targeting all 52 licensed insurance companies in Kenya as per the Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA, 2024) registry, with data collected from Chief Procurement Officers (CPOs), Supply Chain Managers (SCMs), or Operations Managers in each company. The study used a census approach and structured questionnaires with variables measured on a five-point Likert scale. Prior to main data collection, a pilot study involving 10% of the target population validated the research instrument, with Cronbach's Alpha confirming internal consistency. Of the 52 questionnaires administered, 46 were properly completed and returned, representing a response rate of 88.5%. Data were analysed using SPSS version 25.0, applying descriptive statistics and inferential statistics, including Pearson's correlation, multiple linear regression, and ANOVA. Diagnostic tests, specifically the Variance Inflation Factor for multicollinearity, the Shapiro-Wilk test for normality, the Breusch-Pagan test for heteroscedasticity, and the Durbin-Watson statistic for autocorrelation, were conducted before regression analysis and confirmed that the model assumptions were satisfied. Findings: The regression results showed that the supply chain infrastructure context (β = 0.381, B = 0.275, t = 3.490, p = 0.001) made a positive and statistically significant contribution to procurement policy implementation. Supply chain infrastructure context emerged as the strongest predictor of procurement policy implementation, followed by supplier network structure context, information sharing and integration context, and market dynamics context. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: Theoretically, the study validates Institutional Theory in explaining how insurance companies adapt procurement policies to regulatory and market pressures, while confirming the need to integrate the Resource-Based View, Technology Acceptance Model, and Transaction Cost Theory to fully account for the infrastructure, network, and information-sharing dimensions of procurement policy implementation. In practice, the study recommends that insurance company management prioritise investment in integrated electronic procurement infrastructure covering the complete procurement cycle, supplier network development, and information-sharing systems. At the policy level, the study recommends that industry regulators and procurement professionals strengthen market risk management guidance to support procurement policy implementation across the sector.

title: ESG obligations in international commercial contracts: Nature, enforceability and interpretation
summary: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) obligations are increasingly included in international commercial contracts; however, their legal nature and enforceability remain unclear (Joseph & Kyriakakis, 2023). With increasing regulatory, investor, and reputational pressure on multinational enterprises, a key research question is whether, despite the increasing inclusion of ESG clauses, the legal interpretation and enforceability across borders remain to be determined. This paper examines the incorporation of ESG obligations into international commercial contracts, assesses the legal implications, and outlines the challenges related to enforceability. Using a doctrinal, comparative, normative, and practical approach, this paper analyses hard law instruments, such as the Directive (EU) 2024/1760 on Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence and the Modern Slavery Acts, and soft law instruments, including the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs) (United Nations Human Rights Council, 2011) and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises on Responsible Business Conduct (OECD, 2023). The findings suggest that enforceability relies on clear drafting, legally binding obligations, applicable legal principles, key performance indicators (KPIs), monitoring and auditing procedures, and mechanisms for non-compliance. The paper concludes that ESG clauses can gain legal enforceability when integrated into a contractual structure. It offers practical insights for multinational enterprises, lawyers, and policymakers by identifying ways to improve contractual enforceability and ensure that business practices are compliant with new transnational sustainability standards.

title: Human–Artificial Intelligence Collaboration and Green Innovation of Chinese Enterprises: A Digital Perspective
summary: The deep synergy between artificial intelligence and human capital facilitates enterprise green innovation transformation. Adopting the TOE framework, this paper constructs theoretical hypotheses and uses the panel data of Chinese listed firms to explore how human–artificial intelligence collaboration affects green innovation quantity and quality, along with its mediating paths and boundary conditions. Empirical results show that: (1) Human–artificial intelligence collaboration significantly promotes green innovation quantity and quality with quantile heterogeneity. High-innovation enterprises show stronger gains in green innovation quality, while cross-quantile differences are limited for green innovation quantity. (2) Organizational and employee digital capabilities act as mediators. However, the organizational digital capabilities path is not statistically significant for green innovation quantity, whereas other mediating paths are supported. (3) The promotional effect is shaped by digital infrastructure thresholds. Enterprise digital infrastructure produces a double-threshold increasing effect, and regional digital infrastructure creates a single threshold. Past this regional threshold, the effect on green innovation quantity turns from negative to positive. The regional threshold for green innovation quality is marginally significant, with its positive effect only present under low regional digital infrastructure and disappearing once the threshold is crossed. This paper identifies the digital constraints of human–artificial intelligence collaboration for green innovation and provides practical implications for enterprise digital and green development.

title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance dan Intellectual Capital Terhadap Kinerja Keuangan pada IDX30 yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: ABSTRACT This study looks at how intellectual capital and sound corporate governance affect the financial performance of companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange's IDX30 index between 2022 and 2024. Using a purposive sampling technique, non-financial businesses that were included in the IDX30 index for at least two consecutive periods and submitted fully audited annual reports were chosen. This produced a sample of 16 businesses that were monitored throughout a three-year period, giving a total of 48 data points. Return on Assets (ROA) reflected financial performance, intellectual capital was measured using the Value Added Intellectual Coefficient (VAIC) technique, and the percentage of independent commissioners acted as a stand-in for sound corporate governance. Multiple linear regression, classical assumption tests, and hypothesis testing (t-test and F-test) utilizing SPSS software were used for the analysis. According to the findings, effective corporate governance had a coefficient of -0.134 and a significance level of 0.211 (>0.05), indicating that it had no discernible impact on financial performance. On the other hand, intellectual capital demonstrated a positive and significant impact on financial performance with a coefficient of 0.019 and a significance level of 0.000 (<0.05). With an R2 value of 0.379, effective corporate governance and intellectual capital had a substantial impact on financial success when examined concurrently. This means that the two factors together accounted for 37.9% of the observed variation in financial performance. Keywords: Good Corporate Governance, Intellectual Capital, Financial Performance. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini mengkaji bagaimana modal intelektual dan tata kelola perusahaan yang baik memengaruhi kinerja keuangan perusahaan yang terdaftar dalam indeks IDX30 Bursa Efek Indonesia antara tahun 2022 dan 2024. Perusahaan sektor non-keuangan yang secara konsisten masuk dalam indeks IDX30 selama setidaknya dua periode berturut-turut dan memiliki laporan tahunan teraudit yang lengkap dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling; proses ini menghasilkan sampel sebanyak 16 perusahaan yang diamati selama tiga tahun, sehingga diperoleh total 48 observasi. Kinerja keuangan diukur menggunakan Return on Assets (ROA), tata kelola perusahaan yang baik direpresentasikan oleh persentase komisaris independen, dan modal intelektual diukur menggunakan pendekatan Value Added Intellectual Coefficient (VAIC). Analisis yang dilakukan mencakup regresi linear berganda, uji asumsi klasik, serta uji hipotesis (uji-t dan uji-F) dengan menggunakan perangkat lunak SPSS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tata kelola perusahaan yang efektif tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap kinerja keuangan, dengan nilai koefisien -0,134 dan tingkat signifikansi 0,211 (>0,05). Di sisi lain, modal intelektual menunjukkan dampak positif yang kuat terhadap kinerja keuangan dengan nilai koefisien 0,019 dan tingkat signifikansi 0,000 (<0,05). Dengan nilai R2 sebesar 0,379, tata kelola perusahaan yang efektif dan modal intelektual terbukti memiliki pengaruh signifikan terhadap kinerja keuangan ketika diuji secara bersama-sama. Hal ini berarti bahwa kombinasi kedua faktor tersebut menjelaskan 37,9% dari variasi kinerja keuangan. Kata kunci: : Good Corporate Governance, Intellectual Capital, Kinerja Keuangan.

title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance, Kepemilikan Manajerial dan Ukuran Perusahaan Terhadap Nilai Perusahaan
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dampak dari Good Corporate Governance, Kepemilikan Manajerial, dan Ukuran Perusahaan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan. Penelitian ini dilakukan dengan menganalisis laporan keuangan Perusahaan-perusahaan pada sektor perbankan yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) selama periode 2019 hingga tahun 2024 dengan menggunakan teknik pengambilan sampel purposive sampling. Data yang digunakan pada penelitian ini adalah data sekunder berupa laporan keuangan dari setiap Perusahaan yang telah dijadikan sampel penelitian. Variabel yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini yaitu Good Corporate Governance (X1) sebagai variabel bebas pertama, Kepemilikan Manajerial (X2) sebagai variabel bebas kedua, dan Ukuran Perusahaan (X3) sebagai variabel bebas ketiga, serta Nilai Perusahaan (Y) sebagai variabel terikat. title: The information relevance of GAAP-based aggregate spending measures for state economic growth
summary: This study investigates the relevance of state governments' aggregate spending, as reported in audited GAAP-based financial statements, to state economic performance. Utilizing a dynamic panel model to address endogeneity and heterogeneity concerns, the study examines the informativeness of full-accrual and modified-accrual accounting measures for governmental activities and full-accrual accounting measures for business-type activities. The results reveal a negative and statistically significant association between GAAP-based spending measures and state economic growth, suggesting that these measures contain information about economic performance. Additionally, controlling for state-specific heterogeneity enhances the model's explanatory power by 18%, underscoring the importance of accounting for cross-sectional differences in state economies. The findings do not provide evidence that full-accrual measures offer incremental informational relevance beyond modified-accrual measures in explaining state economic growth, consistent with the Governmental Accounting Standards Board's (GASB) view that modified-accrual accounting is more relevant for evaluating short-term fiscal performance. This study highlights the advantages of audited, GAAP-based financial statement data over fiscal data sources that are not independently audited, emphasizing the credibility and consistency of audited reports. The research contributes to the literature by demonstrating the critical role of governmental financial reporting in explaining economic outcomes and promoting public accountability. The results offer important implications for policymakers and standard-setters, suggesting that GAAP-based financial reporting facilitates more informed decision-making regarding resource allocation in state governments.

title: Systematization of the components of the digital transformation mechanism for managing national economic development
summary: The article examines the theoretical foundations for developing a digital transformation mechanism to manage national economic development. The article summarizes existing scholarly approaches to interpreting the concept of a “mechanism,” with particular attention to its systemic and process-oriented nature and its specific application in the context of digital transformation. The article analyzes contemporary approaches to defining and structuring digital transformation mechanisms at different levels of governance, enabling identification of differences in their structural composition, functional purpose, and logic of interaction. The concept of a “digital transformation mechanism for managing the development of the national economy” is refined with due regard to the systemic nature of digital transformation, its strategic orientation, and the interdependence of its components. The study supports systematizing the mechanism’s components by functional purpose. It proposes distinguishing institutional, organizational, financial and economic, technological, human resources, and analytical mechanisms. The study defines their functional purposes and complementary nature in implementing digital transformation processes. The effectiveness of the mechanism depends on the coherence of interaction among its components and their capacity to ensure the achievement of the strategic goals of national economic development. The importance of analytical support for monitoring, performance assessment, identifying deviations, and adjusting managerial decisions is emphasized, thereby creating a feedback loop within the digital transformation process. The proposed systematization provides a basis for further specifying the instrumental content of individual components of the mechanism, identifying their relationship with the strategic goals of digital transformation, and assessing the effectiveness of digital transformation processes. Keywords: digital transformation, national economy, digital transformation mechanism, development management, component, systematization.

title: Implementasi Prosedur Audit Aset Tetap pada Puskesmas oleh KAP Kuncara Budi Santosa dan Rekan
summary: This study aims to analyze the implementation of fixed asset audit procedures conducted by Kuncara Budi Santosa and Associates Public Accounting Firm at a Community Health Center (Puskesmas) with Regional Public Service Agency (BLUD) status. Fixed assets are an important component in public sector financial reporting because their management affects the reliability and accountability of financial statements. This study uses a qualitative descriptive approach. Data were collected through interviews with auditors and direct observation during the audit process. The results show that audit procedures include obtaining asset data and supporting documents, preparing audit working papers, reviewing and reconciling asset records, performing physical inspections, testing capitalization and depreciation, evaluating internal controls, and concluding audit results. Overall, the procedures implemented provided sufficient audit evidence to evaluate the fairness of fixed asset presentation.

title: THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL SUPPLY CHAIN INTEGRATION ON SUSTAINABLE LOGISTICS PERFORMANCE: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF ORGANIZATIONAL RESILIENCE
summary: This study examined the impact of digital supply chain integration on sustainable logistics performance and investigated the mediating role of organizational resilience. The study was significant because sustainable logistics increasingly requires organizations to integrate digital technologies with resilient organizational capabilities to improve operational efficiency, adaptability, and long-term sustainability. A quantitative research design was adopted, and data were collected through a structured, adopted questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. The study was conducted among supply-chain and logistics professionals in Pakistan and a sample of 297 respondents was selected through purposive sampling. The findings showed that digital supply chain integration was positively associated with sustainable logistics performance and organizational resilience, while organizational resilience also demonstrated a positive relationship with sustainable logistics performance. The findings further indicated that organizational resilience partially mediated the relationship between digital supply chain integration and sustainable logistics performance, demonstrating that digital integration contributes to sustainable logistics both directly and through enhanced organizational resilience. These findings are consistent with previous research emphasizing the importance of digital integration, information sharing, supply-chain capabilities, and resilience in achieving sustainable performance. Hence, the study concludes that combining digital supply chain integration with organizational resilience can provide an effective pathway for improving sustainable logistics performance in organizations operating in emerging economies.

title: Cognitive Causal Modeling of Blockchain Adoption in Agri-Food Supply Chains: A Fuzzy-DEMATEL Approach
summary: Background / Introduction: Blockchain can improve agri-food supply-chain transparency, but adoption decisions are cognitively complex because managers judge interdependent criteria under uncertainty. This study frames adoption as cognitive causal decision modeling, aligning with cognitive computation through expert judgment, linguistic uncertainty, causal reasoning, and explainable decision support. Methods: We applied Fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (Fuzzy-DEMATEL) to judgments from 20 experts. Eight technology-adoption criteria were modeled using triangular fuzzy numbers, and an impact relationship map was used to classify criteria by outgoing influence (R), incoming influence (C), prominence (R + C), and net causality (R − C). Results: Smart Contracts showed the strongest net causal influence (R = 3.46; R − C = + 0.78). Food Traceability was the most prominent criterion (R + C = 6.40) and the most influenced by other criteria (C = 3.17). Smart Contracts, Payment Transactions, Food Traceability, Fraud Prevention, and Secure Storage were net causes, whereas Food Waste Prevention, Carbon Emission Detection, and Power Consumption were net effects. Sensitivity analysis confirmed a stable cause/effect partition across threshold and prominence-cutoff variation, with Fraud Prevention the only criterion whose sign reverses at the lower fuzzy bound. Payment Transactions and Secure Storage sit close to the core-driving boundary. Conclusions: The findings support an explainable prioritization logic: transactional and information-security capabilities should be addressed before downstream sustainability outcomes. Because the evidence is expert-elicited rather than longitudinal field performance data, the results should be interpreted as structured decision-support guidance.

title: Youth's Skills Empowerment in the Era of Digital Economy: Prospects and Challenges of Developing Countries
summary: Technological transformation brings significant changes in the dynamics of the global economy, including the digital economy. The digital economy brings a new dimension to economic activities through digitalization. Through the digital economy, people, including young individuals, have great opportunities to take advantage of its benefits. The ease of economic activity, which is quick and efficient, is a chance the community can utilize. Some economic activities, such as e-commerce, provide opportunities for youth to play an active role in the economy. However, in practice, the presence of the digital economy also offers several challenges for youth to take advantage of the digital economy. Barriers such as access to technology and digital skills are still the biggest challenges in developing countries, including Southeast Asian countries. Therefore, this study aims to analyze efforts to empower youth skills in the digital field, especially in the digital economy. Secondary data derived from journal articles, reports, and internet articles are used to support the analysis in this study. From the data findings obtained, it is concluded that there is a need to strengthen several youth skills, such as skills related to digital technology, entrepreneurial skills, financial literacy, and logical thinking. Youth skill empowerment involves all stakeholders, including the government, educational institutions, and the private sector.

title: Digital Economy Spatial Correlation Network and Green Efficiency of Water Resources in China
summary: Within the framework of green sustainable development, the relationship between the digital economy (DE) and the green efficiency of water resources (GEWR) has received increasing attention. This study uses panel data from 30 provincial-level regions in China covering 2014–2023, comprising 300 province-year observations. The objective of this study is to examine the relationship between the digital economy spatial correlation network and GEWR and to explore the potential pathway and moderating role of environmental regulation. Accordingly, it is hypothesized that the DESCN is positively associated with GEWR, that industrial structure upgrading (ISU) and water conservancy industry development (WCI) constitute potential pathways related to this association, and that environmental regulation positively moderates the relationship between DC and GEWR. The super-efficiency slacks-based measure (SE-SBM) model serves as the tool for measuring the level of the GEWR. The digital economy spatial correlation network (DESCN) is constructed through a modified gravity model, which helps analyze interregional DE connections and the spatiotemporal characteristics of GEWR. Furthermore, empirical analysis is conducted to thoroughly examine the relationship between the DESCN and GEWR. The results showed that: (1) the degree centrality (DC) of the DESCN was positively and significantly associated with GEWR; (2) DC was positively and significantly associated with ISU and WCI, supporting H2a and H2b at the level of variable relationships but providing only preliminary evidence concerning the proposed pathways because the corresponding indirect effects were not estimated; and (3) the positive and statistically significant interaction between DC and environmental regulation (ER) indicates that ER strengthens the positive relationship between DC and GEWR.

title: Digital Transformation and Its Influence on Socio‐Economic Dynamics in the Context of the European Union
summary: ABSTRACT Digitalization is reshaping labour markets across the European Union, but its employment implications vary considerably among regions with different economic, technological, innovative and socio‐economic characteristics. This study examines the relationship between digitalization and employment using a balanced panel of 242 EU NUTS2 regions observed between 2011 and 2023, comprising 3146 region‐year observations. The analysis considers regular internet use, employment in high‐technology sectors, R&D expenditure, regional GDP and the at‐risk‐of‐poverty rate. The empirical strategy combines a two‐way fixed‐effects model with NUTS2‐clustered standard errors, a fixed‐effects specification with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and a two‐step System GMM estimator. The results show that regular internet use is consistently associated with regional employment across all specifications, although its economic magnitude is limited. Regional employment exhibits substantial temporal persistence, whereas the estimated contributions of socio‐economic vulnerability, high‐technology specialization and R&D expenditure vary between the static and dynamic models. These findings indicate that digital adoption alone is insufficient to generate uniform labour‐market improvements, and that regional structural conditions shape the capacity to benefit from technological change. The study contributes to the literature by replacing national averages with harmonized NUTS2 evidence and by distinguishing contemporaneous regional associations from dynamic labour‐market adjustment. From a policy perspective, the results support a differentiated approach that combines selective concentration of frontier technological investment with structured diffusion, workforce development and place‐based capability‐building in less‐developed regions.

title: Conceptual Foundations for Forming a Business Economic Security System under Digital Transformation
summary: The article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations for forming a business economic security system under digital transformation. The article substantiates the dual impact of digitalization on economic security: digital technologies improve business-process transparency, accelerate managerial decision-making, and expand risk-forecasting capabilities, while also increasing dependence on digital infrastructure and exposure to cyber, information, technological, financial, and operational threats. The need to move from fragmented responses to individual threats towards an integrated, risk-oriented and adaptive economic security system is established. Changes in the business risk profile caused by automation, platformisation, cloud technologies, big data and artificial intelligence are systematized. Six interconnected functional contours are proposed: strategic and institutional, financial and economic, digital and cyber, operational, human capital and competence, and information and analytical. A conceptual architecture for forming the system is developed, linking strategic objectives, critical assets and business processes, threat sources, risk assessment, functional security contours, managerial instruments, and performance monitoring. A closed management cycle of identification, assessment, prevention, response, recovery and adaptation is substantiated as a mechanism for feedback and organizational learning. It is argued that system effectiveness should be assessed not only by loss reduction but also by a business’s ability to maintain continuity, restore critical processes, and adapt to changes in the digital environment. The proposed approach shifts economic security from a predominantly protective function to an integrated managerial capability that supports resilience and sustainable business development. Keywords: business economic security, digital transformation, digitalization, digital risks, cybersecurity, risk management, resilience, business processes.

summary: Today’s business environment is characterized by high dynamism, technological change, intensifying competition, the digitization of business processes, and growing societal demands for corporate environmental and social responsibility. Under these conditions, traditional approaches to business development are gradually losing their effectiveness. Enterprises are forced not only to adapt to changes in the external environment but also to create new opportunities for their own development actively. Innovative development is becoming a key factor in corporate competitiveness; it involves the creation and implementation of new products, technologies, business models, management approaches, and organizational solutions. At the same time, modern innovations must align with the principles of sustainable development – that is, they must ensure the company’s economic efficiency without excessive use of natural resources or negative impacts on society. The article argues that contemporary challenges related to stricter environmental requirements, corporate social responsibility, and the need to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) create a need for new approaches to managing corporate innovation activities. A matrix is developed to illustrate the interrelationships among the stages of innovation, the Sustainable Development Goals, and ESG components, ensuring the integration of sustainable development principles throughout the innovation process. The practical significance of the results lies in the feasibility of applying the proposed approach to formulating corporate innovation strategies, evaluating the effectiveness of innovation activities, developing ESG policies, and enhancing corporate competitiveness in the context of sustainable development.

title: Building Circular Economy Capabilities: A Systematic Review of Drivers, Practices, Digital Enablers, and Sustainable Outcomes
summary: This study aims to analyze the development of circular economy capabilities and explain the driving factors, organizational capabilities, circular practices, and sustainability outcomes that are relevant to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). The research uses a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) combined with bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed publications for the 2010-2026 period. The initial search yielded 402,309 documents. After the process of checking and eliminating duplication in the selected dataset, 35 unique articles were obtained, with 20 articles explicitly discussing the circular economy, circularity, circular supply chain, or circular business model. The results show that circular economy capabilities are not formed as a single ability, but develop through the interaction between innovation capabilities, collaboration, digitalization, knowledge management, governance, and organizational capabilities. Digitalization plays an enabling role that strengthens the implementation of circular practices when supported by organizational readiness and strategic capabilities. Practices identified include resource use reduction, reuse, material recovery, recycling, circular design, backflow management, and circular business model development. The research synthesis resulted in an integrative framework driving → circular economy capabilities → circular practices → sustainable outcomes. Sustainable outcomes include improved resource efficiency, waste and emissions reduction, supply chain resilience, economic performance, and business resilience. This study expands the understanding of the circular economy from a practice-based approach to an organizational capability perspective and shows that empirical evidence specifically addressing MSMEs is still limited, opening up space for further research.

title: Pengaruh Kepemilikan Institusional, Financial Distress, dan Pergantian Auditor terhadap Audit Delay
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of institutional ownership, financial distress, and auditor turnover on audit delay. The population in this study was all property, real estate, and building construction companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2018-2023 period. The sample size for this study was 45 companies obtained through purposive sampling. A total of 225 samples were obtained. The data type in this study was secondary data, using quantitative research methods and an associative approach. The analysis technique used was panel data regression with a significance level of 5%. This study, processed using EViews 12 software. The findings suggest that audit timeliness is shaped more by the continuity and effectiveness of audit processes than by ownership structure or financial difficulties. This highlights the importance of well-managed auditor transitions, adequate documentation, and effective communication between management and auditors. Strengthening these practices can support timely financial reporting and improve the reliability of information available to stakeholders.

title: Beyond traditional emissions modelling in high value manufacturing: a hybrid approach for net zero supply chains
summary: Achieving net-zero emissions in high-value manufacturing requires more accurate ways of modelling emissions, particularly Scope 3 emissions across complex supply chains. This study conducts a systematic literature review to critically examine existing modelling approaches within production research and high-value manufacturing supply chains. The review shows that game theory, multi-regional input-output models, and simulation approaches such as system dynamics, discrete event simulation, and agent-based modelling are widely used to enhance emissions modelling. However, these approaches are still largely applied in isolation. This fragmentation limits their ability to capture the dynamic, behavioural, and macroeconomic complexities of global supply chains in high-value manufacturing contexts. Drawing on insights from the review, we propose a conceptual hybrid modelling framework for integrating complementary modelling approaches across production systems, supply chain management, and logistics contexts. We also highlight the enabling role of data analytics in strengthening model integration and supply chain transparency. Finally, we develop an agenda to guide future research in hybrid emissions modelling. This research provides a pathway for translating model outputs into industry-relevant insights, identifying key barriers, and exploring how emerging drivers can support a more adaptive and industry-informed transition to net-zero manufacturing.

title: Artificial Intelligence-enabled value creation and competitive advantage in supply chain management: A dynamic capabilities perspective
summary: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) creates strategic value in supply chain management (SCM) by integrating technological capabilities, organizational agility, and human expertise. Using a mixed-methods design, the study combines quantitative survey data from 250 global supply chain executives with three qualitative industry case studies to develop the Artificial Intelligence–Supply Chain Management (AI-SCM) Value Creation Framework, grounded in Dynamic Capabilities Theory. Organizations with higher AI maturity reported 31.5% higher demand-forecast accuracy and 14.5% lower logistics and freight costs. Qualitative evidence indicates that AI-enabled predictive analytics, adaptive decision-making, and operational integration can strengthen supply chain agility and resilience. AI can function as an embedded strategic capability when supported by organizational readiness, reliable data, and human expertise. However, these benefits are not unconditional. Environmental burdens associated with AI infrastructure and algorithmic management risks, including surveillance and reduced worker autonomy, require responsible governance and meaningful human oversight. AI-enabled value creation is therefore contingent on technological capability, organizational conditions, and responsible human-AI integration. title: Modern slavery remediation in healthcare supply chains through blockchain implementation: a socio-technical systems perspective
summary: Purpose Modern slavery remediation remains a supply chain concern for Australian healthcare organisations, which rely heavily on imported goods with limited upstream visibility. Although blockchain is recognised as a means of enhancing supply chain transparency, little is known about how it can be effectively implemented across organisational boundaries. Taking a socio-technical systems approach, this study investigates how blockchain can support the remediation of modern slavery in healthcare supply chains. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts an abductive approach based on semi-structured interviews with healthcare procurement managers and blockchain experts. The abductive approach enables iterative engagement between theoretical insights and empirical evidence to develop a context-sensitive understanding of blockchain implementation in healthcare supply chains. Findings Blockchain implementation for modern slavery remediation is shaped by the interaction between the social and technical subsystems within a broader macro-environmental context. Healthcare organisations are motivated to implement blockchain by external accountability pressures, modern slavery data governance needs, socially sustainable procurement objectives and proactive risk management. However, implementation is constrained by socio-technical misalignments, including uneven organisational readiness, supplier integration barriers and technology-related challenges. To address these misalignments, the study identifies key enabling mechanisms, including supplier support and capability development, strategic stakeholder collaboration and organisational learning. Originality/value This study provides an early empirical investigation of buyer-initiated blockchain implementation for modern slavery remediation in Australian healthcare supply chains. Moving beyond techno-optimistic and techno-pessimistic perspectives, it demonstrates that blockchain effectiveness is neither guaranteed by technical capabilities nor constrained solely by technological limitations but depends on achieving socio-technical alignment across supply chains.

title: Sustainable Supply Chain Management Practices and Organizational Performance of Public Institutions in Rwanda: A Case of Kigali City
summary: Despite numerous efforts made by Kigali City as a public institution through the management of the use of sustainable supply chain management in terms of sustainable sourcing, green recycling, and clean energy efficiency, the performance remains critical and inadequate. Therefore, the general objective of this research project was to analyze the effect of sustainable supply chain management practices on the organizational performance of public institutions in Rwanda. The following were the three specific objectives of the study: To examine the examine the influence of sustainable sourcing on performance of Kigali City; to analyze the effect of green recycling on performance of Kigali City, to analyze the influence of clean energy efficient on performance of Kigali City as well as to analyze the effect of transportation and urban on performance of Kigali City. To achieve these objectives, literature was reviewed on the subject matter, and two theories was aligned with this research, including resource dependency theory as well as theory of empowerment. Data was collected from 138 employees of Kigali City and they were chosen by using the census sampling technique. Questionnaires, interview guides, and documentation were used as tools for data collection. The data was analyzed using both descriptive and inferential statistics by presenting the findings of respondents through the mean and standard deviation. Findings indicated that holding all the stakeholders management to a constant zero, rehousing project performance will be -.889 percent, a unit increase in the use of sustainable sourcing would lead to increase the performance of City of Kigali at 41.7%, a one percent increase in the use of green recycling would lead the performance of City of Kigali at 61.1%, a one percent increase in the use of clean energy efficient would lead to an increase the performance of City of Kigali at 61.1%, furthermore a one percentage increase in the use of transport and urban planning would lead to 22.2% increase the performance of City of Kigali. Overall, both the Green recycling and Clean energy efficient had the greatest effect on the performance of City of Kigali, followed by sustainable sourcing, as well as transport and urban planning. At 5% level of significance and 95% level of confidence, transport and urban planning had 0.048 level of significance; green recycling had a 0.002 level of significance, sustainable sourcing had a 0.004 level of significance and finally clean energy efficient had 0.007 level of significance.

title: Driving sustainability, resilience, and digitalisation in automotive supply chains: A stochastic maturity model for future-oriented transformation
summary: Digitalisation, resilience, and sustainability are key drivers of contemporary supply chain transformation, requiring organisations to make strategic decisions under conditions of uncertainty. To support such decisions, this paper presents a stochastic maturity model that supports the assessment, prioritisation, and continuous improvement of SCM and logistics megatrends and trends under uncertainty. The proposed model combines a configurable maturity structure with Stochastic Multicriteria Acceptability Analysis (SMAA) and empirical probability distributions to enable uncertainty-aware prioritisation of transformation initiatives while remaining adaptable to organisation-specific contexts and continuously evolving business environments. To evaluate the proposed assessment methodology in practice, nine of its ten phases were implemented at a passenger car manufacturer using a panel of six experts. The automotive industry was selected because of the complexity of its global supply chains and advanced logistics practices, providing a demanding environment for evaluating the proposed model. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed assessment procedure in a real industrial environment and illustrate its potential to support strategic decision-making, prioritise transformation initiatives, and facilitate sustainability-oriented supply chain transformation under conditions of uncertainty.

title: Securing the open-source ecosystem: AI-enhanced and explainable supply chain security for reliable software development
summary: Abstract Modern software supply chains face increasing risks from vulnerable and anomalous dependencies, necessitating automated and interpretable detection methods integrated within Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) workflows. Open-source software (OSS) ecosystems are increasingly targeted by sophisticated attacks—including AI model poisoning, dependency confusion, contributor hijacking, and transitive dependency anomalies—that often evade traditional CVE-centric tools such as Snyk and Dependabot. These reactive solutions are primarily designed for known vulnerabilities and may exhibit high false-positive rates when applied to behavioral anomalies, while also lacking interpretable and actionable guidance for developers. This limitation creates a critical barrier to reliable and secure software development in modern DevSecOps environments. To address this gap, this paper introduces XAI-SCS, an intelligent, explainable decision-support framework for OSS supply chain security that performs metadata-driven behavioral risk assessment to proactively identify anomalous package activity. A hybrid CNN–LSTM–Autoencoder architecture achieves strong anomaly-detection performance on the held-out test set (F1 = 0.91), with low repeated-run variability (mean F1 = 0.90 ± 0.02 across five runs) on a federated dataset of 12,000 npm/PyPI package versions, primarily trained using CVE-linked labels and GAN-simulated poisoning samples. A separate held-out evaluation set of 240 manually curated real-world non-CVE OSS supply-chain incidents was used exclusively for external generalization assessment. Accordingly, the non-CVE results are interpreted as preliminary evidence of transferability to selected metadata-visible behavioral anomalies rather than comprehensive real-world non-CVE threat coverage. To support transparent developer decision-making, SHAP-based explanations and counterfactual remediation suggestions produced high perceived clarity (4.3 ± 0.4/5) and actionability (4.1 ± 0.5/5) and self-reported remediation intent (96%, n = 82). However, these findings reflect developer perceptions in a controlled study and do not yet demonstrate measured improvements in real-world remediation time, fix completion, or vulnerability resolution within operational DevSecOps teams. Optional high-assurance deployment extensions, including Federated Continual Learning, zero-knowledge attestation via zk-SNARKs, and post-quantum secure enclaves, are presented as exploratory architectural pathways for future privacy-preserving, verifiable, and confidential deployment, rather than as part of the core empirical evaluation. Embedded in controlled, CI/CD-representative workflows with 0.8-second average latency, XAI-SCS remains competitive with CVE-centric tools on known-vulnerability cases while providing preliminary evidence of complementary metadata-level behavioral risk screening in GAN-simulated and limited curated non-CVE evaluation subsets. The comparison is therefore interpreted as evidence that XAI-SCS can complement CVE-centric SCA tools by adding metadata-level behavioral screening and developer-facing explanations, rather than replacing or universally outperforming tools such as Snyk and Dependabot. This work’s primary contribution is a metadata-driven, CI/CD-integrated intelligent decision-support framework that delivers high-accuracy behavioral anomaly detection (F1 = 0.91) and transparent, developer-facing explanations (clarity 4.3/5, remediation intent 96%) for OSS supply chain risk assessment. Optional high-assurance deployment extensions (federated learning, cryptographic attestation, secure enclaves) are discussed separately and do not form part of the core empirical evaluation.

title: Too Much Financial Integration: The Perils of Open Capital Accounts in Low and Middle Income Countries
summary: ABSTRACT Over the past 3 decades, financial integration of lower income countries with global capital markets has in most cases been detrimental to development. Currency hierarchies determine investor perceptions and render capital flows to such countries more volatile and more demanding of higher returns. They also lead to significant spillover effects of macroeconomic policies in advanced economies. As a result, financial integration has not led to sustained increases in investment rates or economic growth, has generated greater financial instability and vulnerability, and been associated with high ‘seignorage costs’ because of differences in rates of return of capital inflows and outflows. Developing countries now suffer from ‘too much financial integration’, and cross‐border capital flows should be more regulated.

title: Environmental Environmental Regulation Pressure and Green Innovation Bubbles: Resource Channels and the Amplifying Role of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Environmental regulation may expand visible green-innovation inputs without proportionate contemporaneous patent output. We examine a supplied residual measure of this input–output mismatch in a matched sample of 27,157 observations on 4560 Chinese A-share listed firms from 2014 to 2022. In the industry- and year-adjusted specification, regulatory pressure is positively associated with the residual (0.031, firm-clustered p<0.001). Complete mediation equations identify the WW financing index and environmental investment as exploratory resource channels. Conditional effects of regulatory pressure are positive across the reported AI-disclosure distribution. The magnitude is modest: a one-standard-deviation increase in regulatory pressure corresponds to approximately 0.0066 outcome units, or 0.039 standard deviations. The evidence documents systematic cross-firm covariation and motivates closer attention to input–output conversion. Firm fixed-effects sensitivity and the contemporaneous construction limit within-firm and causal interpretation; future research should validate the construct using forward patent output, patent quality, and physical environmental performance.

title: Design thinking as a practice system for knowledge-enabled digital transformation: microfoundations of dynamic capabilities
summary: Purpose Digital transformation (DT) demands more than technology adoption; it reshapes organisational routines, knowledge and decision structures, and the capabilities firms rely on to compete. Yet many firms fail to move DT beyond pilots, revealing a deeper problem: organisations lack the knowledge mechanisms needed to sustain transformation at scale. Design/methodology/approach This paper positions design thinking (DTk) as a knowledge practice system: an interrelated set of methods, mindsets and artefacts that shapes the microfoundations of dynamic capabilities (DCs) during DT. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 14 practitioners in the Dutch financial services sector, the authors inductively identify and elaborate three DTk-shaped microfoundations: Adapting (sensing through problem framing bounded by strategic intent and short, iterative experiments), Governing (seizing through user evidence, structured decision checkpoints, role clarity and contracting mechanisms) and Conveying (reconfiguring through storytelling, boundary artefacts and shared vocabulary that transfer and translate knowledge across organisational boundaries). Findings The authors demonstrate how these mechanisms address key DT challenges – strategic misalignment, decision risks, legacy-system constraints and cross-functional coordination failures – that are, at their core, knowledge management (KM) challenges. The analysis further specifies the knowledge processes each microfoundation enacts, a configuration logic among the three microfoundations and the failure modes that arise from imbalanced enactment. Practical implications For managers, this paper provides guidance for embedding DTk as a practice system to strengthen knowledge transfer, strategic alignment and coordinated organisational change. Organisations in regulated, legacy-intensive settings are encouraged to emphasise Adapting to manage integration risk, Governing for compliance-robust decisions and Conveying to coordinate across stakeholder groups. Originality/value This paper contributes to DC, DTk and KM literature in four ways, it offers a mechanism-level specification of how DTk practices serve as the microfoundations of DCs during DT; repositions DTk as a knowledge practice system connecting DC theory and KM scholarship; articulates a configuration logic and failure modes arising from imbalanced enactment and incorporates a monitoring loop consistent with capability dynamisation that sustains transformation momentum without disrupting core operations; and identifies boundary conditions as simultaneously KM conditions that intensify specific knowledge processes in highly regulated, legacy-intensive contexts.

title: Stakeholder perspectives on biosecurity adoption in the Colorado cattle supply chain: lessons from foot-and-mouth disease preparedness
summary: Biosecurity is essential to protecting cattle health and maintaining continuity of business during high-consequence disease events, yet adoption of preparedness measures remains uneven across the beef supply chain. Using foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) as a motivating case, we examine how Colorado cattle-industry stakeholders define practical biosecurity and what lessons support preparedness before an emergency. Data were collected through 12 focus groups and 18 individual interviews with 75 stakeholders across nine cattle-industry sectors, followed by four cross-sector workshops with 56 participants. FMD was widely perceived as a distant, low-priority threat, while time, labor, cost, operational scale, traceability burdens, seasonal and geographic constraints, and limited veterinary access shaped what stakeholders considered feasible. Workshop participants identified visitor/vendor hygiene and controlled access as the most feasible measures, while quarantining new or returning animals received the most votes for both impact and urgency, followed by avoiding commingling with animals from other herds (impact) and knowing or asking about disease status of source herds (urgency). Trusted local messengers and cross-sector communication protocols emerged as central to practical, voluntary biosecurity improvement in Colorado. Strengthening biosecurity will require practical tools, trusted communication networks, and cross-sector planning that reflect the day-to-day realities of cattle operations.

title: THE CIRCULAR CREATIVE ECONOMY: SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN COMMERCIAL PHOTOGRAPHY AND DESIGN PRODUCTION
summary: Global economic uncertainty and the climate crisis demand fundamental transformations across various sectors, including the creative industry. Conventional commercial photography and visual communication design production often generate a substantial carbon footprint through material waste, excessive energy consumption, and high logistical mobility. This paper explores the integration of circular economy principles and digital transformation within visual production workflows as a strategic response to these sustainability challenges. This research aims to analyze how the adoption of disruptive technologies - such as generative artificial intelligence, virtual production, and cloud computing - can reduce carbon emissions while simultaneously enhancing operational cost efficiency. The methodology employs a systematic literature review alongside qualitative case studies of creative agencies that have implemented sustainable workflows. Findings indicate that the digitalization of creative processes effectively eliminates physical waste, notably excessive sample printing and single-use practical set constructions. Furthermore, the transition toward a virtual production ecosystem is proven to drastically minimize logistical expenses, thereby bolstering the financial resilience of industry practitioners amidst a fragmented global economy. Leveraging cutting-edge technology also substantially accelerates project turnaround times without compromising aesthetic design quality. In conclusion, the adoption of digital technologies is not merely a fleeting aesthetic trend but an essential catalyst for establishing a circular and inclusive creative economy. This innovative transformation empowers visual communication designers and professional photographers to remain productive, relevant, and highly competitive globally. Ultimately, these crucial economic milestones can be achieved while practitioners uphold strong ethical responsibilities toward ecological preservation and the development of future-proof business models.

title: The Effect of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) on the Audit Efficiency of Selected Banks in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the effect of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) on audit efficiency in selected banks in Nigeria, with emphasis on fraud detection and risk management. Audit efficiency was measured using average audit report lag. The study adopted an ex post facto research design and relied on secondary data obtained from published financial statements, annual reports, and regulatory disclosures of 10 selected banks in Nigeria for the period 2010 to 2025. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data, while panel unit root tests were conducted to establish stationarity. Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression analysis was then employed to test the effect of RPA-related variables on audit efficiency. The findings showed that RPA in fraud detection had a significant negative effect on audit report lag, indicating that automation enhances audit efficiency by reducing the time required to complete audit engagements. Furthermore, RPA in risk management, proxied by the average nonperforming loan ratio, is statistically significant effect on audit efficiency. The study concludes that RPA contributes more strongly to audit efficiency when applied to fraud detection than to risk management activities. The study recommends that banks increase investment in RPA-driven fraud detection systems and improve the integration of automation tools into their risk management frameworks. The study adds to existing knowledge on digital transformation, audit automation, and technology-enabled auditing in emerging economies.

title: Climate Transition-Risk Salience and the Financial Relevance of Reported Green Supply Chain Management Practices: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
summary: The transition toward a low-carbon economy requires firms to extend sustainability considerations beyond their organizational boundaries and into supply chain operations. Yet the financial relevance of reported green supply chain management (GSCM) practice breadth may vary with the prominence of climate transition issues in corporate reporting. Drawing on the natural-resource-based view and the attention-based view, this study examines whether reported climate transition-risk salience (CTRS) conditions the association between reported GSCM practice breadth and subsequent accounting profitability. The analysis uses 26,132 firm-year observations from 4371 Chinese listed firms. A seven-item index of reported GSCM practice breadth and an annual-report-based measure of CTRS for 2016–2023 are linked to return on assets (ROA) in the following financial year. Firm- and outcome-year fixed-effects estimates provide qualified support for a positive average association. In the preferred controlled specification, a one-standard-deviation increase in reported GSCM practice breadth is associated with an approximately 0.17-percentage-point increase in subsequent ROA. This economically modest estimate remains sensitive to the control structure, particularly the inclusion of firm size. The moderating relationship is more consistent. The estimated association between reported GSCM practice breadth and subsequent ROA is statistically imprecise at low reported CTRS, reaches approximately 0.15 percentage points at mean salience, and increases to approximately 0.29 percentage points at the 90th percentile. The positive interaction remains stable across alternative GSCM and CTRS measures, environmental-reporting controls, temporal diagnostics, and additional fixed-effects specifications. In common-sample comparisons, the GSCM–CTRS interaction is more positive than the corresponding interactions with physical climate-risk exposure assigned according to firms’ registered provinces and cities. These comparisons remain subject to differences in risk content and measurement level. The findings identify reported climate transition-risk salience as a boundary condition for the association between reported GSCM practice breadth and subsequent profitability. This conditional perspective connects supply chain sustainability with the firm’s reported climate transition context while preserving the distinction between reported practice breadth and implementation quality.

title: Does international supply shock necessitate supply chain diversification? Evidence from China’s imports of intermediate goods
summary: This paper examines the impact of international intermediate input supply shocks on firms’ supply chain diversification and its adjustment direction. Using Chinese firm-level customs data from 2009 to 2016, we find a significant U-shaped relationship between supply shocks and supply chain diversification. When shocks are relatively weak, firms tend to maintain concentrated supply chains due to cost and efficiency considerations. Once shocks exceed a certain threshold, firms increase diversification to mitigate risks. Further analysis shows that firms adjust not only the degree but also the direction of supply chain diversification. In response to supply shocks, firms shift from efficiency-oriented to security-oriented sourcing strategies, increasing imports from countries with regional trade agreements, Belt and Road participation, and lower geopolitical risks, while reducing dependence on politically distant or disaster-prone regions. This paper reveals the dynamic trade-off underlying firms’ supply chain decisions and provides micro-level evidence for understanding how firms in emerging economies respond to global supply disruptions.

title: Digitization tools as a basis for improving the accounting and taxation of an agrarian enterprise
summary: The article examines the theoretical-methodical and applied principles of digitalization of accounting and taxation in an agrarian enterprise amid increasing information volumes, more complex economic processes, and the need for operational information support for management decisions. It is substantiated that the digitalization of accounting and tax activities should be considered not only as the automation of individual operations, but as a complex process of forming an integrated information environment of the enterprise. The main digitalization tools include primary accounting, electronic document management, accounting and tax accounting, electronic reporting, digital control, analytics, and management. The peculiarities of their application in the agricultural sector are defined by production seasonality, the territorial dispersion of economic processes, the large volume of primary documents, and the need to record production data in real time. The study proposes a conceptual model for the integrated digitalization of accounting and taxation in an agrarian enterprise, establishing consistent relationships among primary accounting, electronic document flow, a single information base, accounting and tax accounting, electronic reporting, digital control, BI analytics, and management decisions, with feedback loops. The study proposes guidelines for evaluating the effectiveness of digitization based on time, quality, cost, tax, information, management, and personnel criteria. The study identifies the main risks of digital transformation and proposes a step-by-step implementation approach. The study shows that integrating digital tools improves the efficiency and reliability of accounting and tax information, reduces labor intensity and tax risks, and improves the quality of management decisions. Keywords: digitization; accounting; tax accounting; agricultural enterprise; digital tools; electronic document management; tax reporting; digital control; information support; management decisions.

title: Peran Moderasi ESG Risk Rating dan Beta dalam Estimasi Nilai Perusahaan (The Moderating Role of ESG Risk Rating and Beta in Firm Value Estimation)
summary: Studi ini menginvestigasi peran moderasi Peringkat Risiko ESG (ESG Risk Rating) dan Beta saham dalam memengaruhi hubungan antara struktur modal, kinerja keuangan, dan nilai perusahaan. Populasi riset mencakup perusahaan yang terdaftar dalam indeks ESG Leaders di IDX 2020–2025. Melalui pendekatan purposive sampling, sejumlah 15 perusahaan berhasil diidentifikasi sebagai sampel representatif. Analisis dengan FEM dan MRA. Temuan kunci struktur modal signifikan dengan nilai perusahaan, sementara kinerja keuangan tidak memperlihatkan pengaruh yang substansial. Selanjutnya, Peringkat Risiko ESG tidak terbukti memoderasi efek struktur modal, kinerja keuangan dengan nilai perusahaan. Sebaliknya, Beta saham ditemukan memiliki peran moderasi yang signifikan dengan melemahkan dampak kinerja keuangan dengan nilai perusahaan, tidak demikian halnya dengan struktur modal. Secara inferensial, hasil ini menyiratkan bahwa investor domestik cenderung kurang mempertimbangkan risiko keberlanjutan jangka panjang dan lebih responsif terhadap dinamika risiko pasar riil dalam proses evaluasi ekuitas korporasi

title: Staged digital transformation and firms’ total factor productivity: evidence from Chinese cultural firms
summary: This study explores the effects of digital transformation (DT) on firms’ total factor productivity (TFP) across the digital technology application (DTA) stage and digital business model innovation (DBMI) stage. Using a sample of 245 Chinese listed cultural firms from 2011 to 2022, we examine how DT impacts TFP differently across these stages. The results show that DT significantly enhances firms’ TFP in both the DTA and DBMI stages. However, productivity gains materialize only after firms reach the transformation threshold in both stages. Moreover, the threshold for the DTA stage is higher than that for the DBMI stage. In the DTA stage, DT improves firms’ TFP by enhancing their core production capabilities and specialization. In the DBMI stage, DT affects firms’ TFP through improved operational efficiency and financial efficiency. Furthermore, during the DTA stage, larger firms experience stronger TFP gains, while smaller firms benefit more in the DBMI stage. In the DTA stage, the positive impact of DT on TFP is similar for firms with and without government subsidies. In the DBMI stage, however, the impact of DT is more pronounced for firms without subsidies. Across both stages, firms in regions with a better digital financial environment achieve greater productivity gains from DT.

title: Pengaruh Green Accounting, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), Ukuran Perusahaan, dan Profitabilitas terhadap Nilai Perusahaan Tambang yang terdaftar di BEI Tahun 2022–2025
summary: This research is motivated by the increasing demand for the implementation of sustainable business practices in mining companies and the fluctuation of firm value, which highlights the importance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure, Green Accounting, firm size, and profitability as factors affecting firm value. This study aims to analyze the effect of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), Green Accounting, firm size, and profitability on the firm value of mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2022–2025 period. The study employs a quantitative approach with an associative research design. The data used are secondary data obtained from the companies’ annual reports and sustainability reports and analyzed using panel data regression. The sample was selected through a purposive sampling technique, resulting in 48 observations. The results indicate that ESG, Green Accounting, and firm size have no significant effect on firm value, while profitability has a positive and significant effect on firm value. Simultaneously, all four variables have a significant effect on firm value. These findings suggest that profitability remains the primary determinant of firm value in the mining sector, and the results may serve as a consideration for corporate management, investors, and regulators in making decisions related to sustainability practices and firm value enhancement.

title: The digital transformation paradox: how organizational and institutional barriers neutralize leadership investment in systemic banking
summary: Purpose This study examines the “digital transformation paradox” in which systemic banks invest heavily in technology yet remain digitally immature. It identifies and prioritizes the key technological, organizational, and institutional barriers that constrain transformation despite strong leadership commitment. Ultimately, the paper reframes digital transformation from a problem of execution to a problem of institutional design. Design/methodology/approach The study applies a hybrid Delphi–scaling methodology with senior experts from Greece’s four systemic banks. It integrates Institutional Theory with an extended Technology–Organization–Environment–Value (TOE–V) framework. A Delphi process established consensus on 14 major inhibitors, followed by a scaling survey that ranked their relative impact. Findings The results reveal a persistent transformation trap driven by legacy information technology (IT) systems, rigid organizational routines, and compliance-focused governance. These factors redirect modernization toward regulatory conformity rather than operational improvement. Clear and enforceable regulatory mandates, however, can act as catalysts for modernization. Digital maturity should be assessed not only in terms of adoption but also in terms of outcomes, including usability, personalisation, and relevance to stakeholders. Practical implications Executives should move beyond viewing transformation as primarily a technology initiative and address structural constraints such as technical debt and cultural resistance, and tie digital investments to measurable stakeholder outcomes. Originality/value The study conceptualizes the digital transformation paradox as a systemic outcome of organizational and institutional constraints. It extends the TOE framework through TOE–V by showing how value realization conditions digital maturity in regulated environments, repositioning digital transformation as a challenge of institutional design rather than execution.

title: 19. Digital Governance and State Capacity in Africa: Institutional Challenges in Public-Sector Digital Transformation
summary: The drive towards digital transformation has been a growing part of the agenda for public-sector reform in Africa. Governments are implementing various technologies—such as digital identification systems, online public service platforms, electronic payment systems, data-sharing infrastructure, digital procurement systems, etc.—to enhance administrative efficiency, the access to and nature of public services, accountability, and state responsiveness. However, increasing the use of digital government does not necessarily lead to improved state capacity. The success of any digital transformation relies on public organisations' institutional capacity to coordinate digital transformation, fund and sustain digital infrastructure, build skills, create interoperability, secure data, oversee cybersecurity, and integrate digital investments into everyday administrative operations. The article explores the institutional challenges that explain digital transformation in the public sector in Africa, specifically by looking at the link between digital governance and state capacity. Based on evidence from the African Union, the United Nations, the World Bank, the OECD and comparative digital-government datasets, it claims that the flipside of the digitization of technologies is the decentralization of digital government within the state itself. There is persistent evidence of poor interoperability, digital skills, institutional coordination, regulatory capacity, data governance, cyber security, financing, and citizen inclusion. Meanwhile, there have been tangible advances in online service provision, digital identification, digital payments, and common digital infrastructure in Africa. This analysis thus denies a straightforward technologization deficit explanation. Rather, digital transformation is seen as an institutional-capacity challenge in which technology, administrative organisation, regulations, human resources and political coordination play a part. The article concludes that sustainable digital governance needs to foster a holistic approach to coordination among government bodies, interoperable digital public infrastructure (DPI), improved capacities of public sector, institutionalized data governance, cybersecurity capacities and tools for assessing real service use and administrative outcomes.

title: ESG Reporting Practices and Their Impact on Corporate Financial Sustainability
summary: This paper explores the link between ESG reporting and financial sustainability of corporations across different economies. Relying on the synthesis of empirical evidence gathered during 2021-2026, the study explores the impact of the quality of ESG reporting on cost of capital, firm valuation and financial sustainability of firms in the long run. The methodology suggested consists of meta-analytic literature review and panel analysis of firm-level data. The findings reveal a positive connection between high ESG scores and cost of debt and equity that is considerably lower than that of firms with lower ESG scores, especially those related to social and governance dimensions of ESG ratings. Based on meta-analytical evidence based on 60,247 firm-level observations, the results reveal that ESG disclosure lowers the weighted cost of capital and improves market-based performance measures. However, the relationship between disclosure and performance is conditional upon the institutional setting, assurance quality and the nature of ESG involvement.

title: Leveraging HR Analytics Capability for Sustainable Supply Chains: The Roles of Green HRM, AI‐Driven Capabilities and Resource Commitment
summary: ABSTRACT Among many firms in emerging economies, investments in HR analytics promise strategic insight yet often fail to translate into measurable sustainability gains. This study theorises and tests how HR analytics capability drives supply chain sustainability through the strategic enactment of Green HRM (GHRM). Drawing on dynamic capability theory and socio‐technical systems theory, we propose that HR analytics capability indirectly enhances supply chain sustainability by enabling firms to design and implement data‐informed GHRM strategies that align workforce practices with environmental objectives. We further argue that this indirect effect is contingent on two distinct enabling conditions: AI‐driven capability, which strengthens the translation of HR analytics capability into GHRM strategy, and organisational resource commitment, which strengthens the translation of GHRM strategy into sustainable supply chain outcomes. Using two‐wave survey data from 248 owner‐managers and managers of manufacturing SMEs in Ghana, we find support for the mediated relationship between HR analytics capability and supply chain sustainability through GHRM strategy, together with significant first‐stage moderation by AI‐driven capability and second‐stage moderation by organisational resource commitment. The findings advance theory by clarifying the micro foundations through which analytical capabilities shape sustainability performance and by identifying the boundary conditions under which such capabilities yield strategic environmental returns in resource‐constrained contexts.
